title: Graph Neural Networks with Memory-Augmented Attention Mechanisms
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have demonstrated remarkable success in various domains, including social network analysis, drug discovery, and recommender systems. However, a significant limitation of many GNN architectures is their struggle to effectively capture long-range dependencies within graphs. This paper introduces a novel approach that integrates memory-augmented attention mechanisms into GNNs, addressing this limitation. Our model enables nodes to retain and utilize information from past interactions, creating a persistent memory of the graph's evolving state. This allows the network to better understand complex relationships and improve performance on tasks requiring long-range dependency modeling. We detail the architecture, training procedure, and empirical results, showcasing the enhanced capabilities of our proposed method. The core claim of this work is that integrating memory mechanisms significantly improves a GNN's ability to model long-range dependencies.

title: 基于自适应拓扑结构的图神经网络
abstract: This paper introduces a novel graph neural network (GNN) architecture, termed "Adaptive Topology Graph Neural Network" (ATGNN), that leverages the concept of self-adaptive topology to enhance learning and optimization capabilities within complex data environments. Traditional GNNs often struggle to adapt to dynamic data, necessitating static graph representations. The ATGNN dynamically adjusts the graph topology based on the input data, enabling the network to effectively navigate intricate patterns and identify optimal solutions. This paper details the architecture, training methodology, and experimental results demonstrating the ATGNN's superior performance in tasks involving high-dimensional data and complex relationships. The core mechanism centers around the continuous optimization of the graph structure through dynamic topology adjustments, allowing the network to uncover subtle correlations and efficiently navigate challenging data landscapes.

title: Generative AI, Autonomous Agents, and Conversational Marketing for Governance Trust, Agency, and Control
abstract: This chapter examines the evolution of conversational marketing from rule-based chatbots to generative AI and autonomous agents capable of inference, persuasion, optimization, and market-facing execution. It argues that the rise of agentic marketing requires a shift from adoption-centered analysis to a governance-centered perspective that connects personalization, trust, control, and accountability. Drawing on marketing, information systems, communication, organization studies, law, and ethics, the chapter develops the AGTC framework to explain how agency, governance, trust, and control interact across platform, firm, and consumer levels. It also identifies theoretical, methodological, and contextual gaps, especially in emerging markets, multilingual environments, and uneven regulatory settings, while outlining implications for research, managerial strategy, and public policy in the age of autonomous market systems.

title: Do Residents Feel What Seismometers Measure? A Three-Year Panel Experiment Co-Locating Felt Reports with Plug-In Home Seismometers in the Greater Tokyo Metropolitan Area
abstract: Discrepancies between announced regional seismic intensity and shaking experienced indoors may affect household mitigation and risk communication. We report on a three-year field experiment (2021–2024) in the Greater Tokyo Metropolitan Area combining citizen-hosted low-cost sensors with subjective reports. Up to 92 volunteers participated; sensor hosts kept plug-in micro-electromechanical systems (MEMS) seismometers at home, and participants completed questionnaires after 96 target earthquakes. The system yielded 5,724 responses to 8,054 delivery attempts (response rates of 80.6% in 2022 and 67.6% in 2023), with 96% returned within 72 hours. Findings were robust to unrounded measures. First, municipal Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) seismic intensity < perceived seismic intensity < indoor seismic intensity; indoor seismic intensity exceeded municipal JMA seismic intensity by roughly one-third of a class (median +0.34 against unrounded instrumental values), with a 1.4-class variation across structures. Second, local intensity was the primary predictor of feeling an event (odds ratio 2.57 per class), whereas the floor-height association was weaker. Third, repeated feedback did not produce detectable calibration; over-reporting biases (+0.4 to +0.7 classes) persisted over up to 96 events. These findings support indoor seismic intensity as a complement to regional metrics for indoor seismic-hazard evaluation, last-mile early warning, and risk communication.

title: Quantum-Inspired Feature Engineering For Logistic Regression
abstract: Banks predict credit default with Logistic Regression because regulators can read its coefficients—but it cannot express interactions. We add the missing non-linearity with a quantum-inspired feature map: 8 of the data's 23 columns become rotation angles of 8 qubits in an IQP circuit simulated in PennyLane, and 2 × 8 = 16 outputs are appended to the 23. On the UCI Default of Credit Card Clients data (30,000 clients, 5-fold CV) this lifts it from F1 = 0.462 to 0.517, while Kernel PCA, the strongest classical alternative at the same budget, reaches only 0.493; the gap survives FDR correction over 12 tests (p = 0.00007). The gain is specific to linear models: Random Forest, SVM, XGBoost, and k-NN, already non-linear, do not benefit. What caps n is the simulator, holding 2n amplitudes; on hardware the depth is independent of n.

title: WaveSync: Constrained Wavefront Optimization for Synchronized Co-Speech Gestures in Humanoid Robots
abstract: Expressive co-speech gestures are crucial for natural human--robot interaction, yet generating them on physical humanoid robots remains challenging because, unlike virtual avatars, robots must synchronize gestures with speech under strict kinematic and actuator constraints. We present WaveSync, a hybrid framework in which a Large Language Model decomposes dialogue responses into structured semantic schemas and assigns per-word importance weights, forming a continuous Semantic Importance Wave. Gesture trajectories are shaped through Dynamic Movement Primitives to ensure kinematic feasibility while enhancing expressiveness. A Wavefront Optimization stage aligns gesture stroke peaks with speech emphasis peaks and resolves residual temporal conflicts through gesture-duration compression and forward propagation. Experimental evaluation across five dialogue scenarios demonstrates effective gesture--speech alignment and favorable performance in both objective and subjective evaluations. The results further show that the key components of WaveSync contribute to producing gestures that are expressive, semantically grounded, and kinematically feasible. The code, resources, and videos are available at https://github.com/pairs-lab/WaveSync{WaveSync}.

title: Squint: Fast Visual Reinforcement Learning for Sim-to-Real Robotics
abstract: Visual reinforcement learning is appealing for robotics but expensive. Off-policy methods are sample-efficient yet slow while on-policy methods parallelize well but waste samples. Recent work has shown that off-policy methods can train faster than on-policy methods in wall-clock time for state-based control. Extending this to vision remains challenging, where high-dimensional input images complicate training dynamics and introduce substantial storage and encoding overhead. To address these challenges, we introduce Squint, a visual Soft Actor Critic method that achieves faster wall-clock training than prior visual off-policy and on-policy methods. Squint achieves this via parallel simulation, a distributional critic, resolution squinting, layer normalization, a tuned update-to-data ratio, and an optimized implementation. We evaluate on the SO-101 Task Set, a new suite of eight manipulation tasks in ManiSkill3 with heavy domain randomization, and demonstrate sim-to-real transfer to a real SO-101 robot. We train policies for 15 minutes on a single RTX 3090 GPU, with most tasks converging in under 6 minutes.

evidence.title: Squint: Fast Visual Reinforcement Learning for Sim-to-Real Robotics
evidence.abstract: Visual reinforcement learning is appealing for robotics but expensive. Off-policy methods are sample-efficient yet slow while on-policy methods parallelize well but waste samples. Recent work has shown that off-policy methods can train faster than on-policy methods in wall-clock time for state-based control. Extending this to vision remains challenging, where high-dimensional input images complicate training dynamics and introduce substantial storage and encoding overhead. To address these challenges, we introduce Squint, a visual Soft Actor Critic method that achieves faster wall-clock training than prior visual off-policy and on-policy methods. Squint achieves this via parallel simulation, a distributional critic, resolution squinting, layer normalization, a tuned update-to-data ratio, and an optimized implementation. We evaluate on the SO-101 Task Set, a new suite of eight manipulation tasks in ManiSkill3 with heavy domain randomization, and demonstrate sim-to-real transfer to a real SO-101 robot. We train policies for 15 minutes on a single RTX 3090 GPU, with most tasks converging in under 6 minutes.

title: Quantum Entanglement Self-Adaptive Topology
abstract: Quantum entanglement offers a novel approach to topology discovery and optimization, potentially surpassing classical methods. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, "Quantum Entanglement Self-Adaptive Topology," leveraging quantum entanglement to automatically uncover and refine topological structures. The core mechanism hinges on simulating quantum entanglement to guide the evolution of a topological landscape, leading to efficient structural analysis and data compression. The algorithm's potential impact spans physical simulations and data compression, offering a paradigm shift in computational paradigms.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Network Model Adjustment
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive model adjustment framework based on quantum networks, leveraging quantum entanglement and superposition to dynamically adjust model parameters. The proposed method aims to enhance model performance and generalization capabilities through automated parameter optimization. We present a theoretical analysis of the potential benefits and challenges of this approach, outlining the key mechanisms and potential improvements. The core claim centers on the utilization of quantum phenomena to automate model parameter tuning, representing a significant departure from traditional optimization techniques. This research explores the implications of this approach on various machine learning tasks, demonstrating its potential for improved generalization and performance.

title: Probability Logic Nonlinear Geometry (PLNG) Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Probability Logic Nonlinear Geometry (PLNG) framework designed to model complex geometric structures and leverage probabilistic reasoning for enhanced modeling capabilities. We propose a framework that integrates probability logic with geometric modeling, incorporating a dynamic evolution mechanism and probabilistic models to capture the intricate patterns and transformations inherent in geometric phenomena. The core mechanism involves a structured approach to represent and analyze geometric evolution, leveraging the power of probability to provide a more robust and interpretable model. This work offers a new perspective on geometric modeling, moving beyond traditional approaches to provide a more flexible and powerful tool for understanding and predicting geometric behavior.

title: Quantum-Aware Constraint Propagation for Molecular Dynamics
abstract: This paper introduces a novel constraint propagation technique for molecular dynamics simulations that incorporates quantum effects to enhance accuracy and reduce computational cost. Traditional constraint propagation methods often rely on classical algorithms, which can be computationally expensive and limit the resolution of simulations. We propose a quantum-inspired approach that utilizes quantum entanglement to represent and manipulate molecular configurations, leading to improved accuracy and reduced computational demands. The paper details the theoretical foundations of this approach, provides a comprehensive implementation of the constraint propagation algorithm, and explores its performance evaluation against established methods. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in simulation accuracy and reduced computational time, showcasing the potential of this method for advancing molecular dynamics research.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Circuit Design
abstract: This paper investigates the application of reinforcement learning (RL) to the adaptive design of electronic circuits. Traditional circuit design is a highly iterative and often manual process, requiring significant expertise and time investment. This research proposes a novel approach where an RL agent is trained to automatically generate circuit designs that satisfy pre-defined performance specifications. The agent interacts with a circuit simulator, receiving rewards based on the quality of the designed circuit and penalized for deviations from the target specifications. The core of the system relies on a Markov Decision Process (MDP) formulation, where the state represents the circuit design, the action represents a design modification, and the reward reflects the circuit's performance. The algorithm utilizes a Deep Q-Network (DQN) architecture to learn an optimal policy for selecting actions. The results demonstrate the potential of RL to automate complex circuit design tasks, potentially leading to faster design cycles and the creation of circuits with optimized performance. The effectiveness of this approach is evaluated through simulations and showcases the ability of RL to learn designs that surpass those achieved through conventional design methods. Further research will focus on scaling the approach to larger and more complex circuits and incorporating constraints related to manufacturability and cost.

title: Automated Discovery of Mathematical Identities from Code
abstract: The discovery of mathematical identities—relationships between mathematical expressions—is a cornerstone of mathematical research. However, this process is traditionally a laborious, manual endeavor, often requiring significant human effort in pattern recognition, symbolic manipulation, and verification. This paper presents an automated system designed to tackle this challenge. The core of our approach leverages program synthesis techniques in conjunction with symbolic execution to derive mathematical identities directly from code snippets. We formulate the problem as a search for equations that accurately represent the logic of the code. The system explores different equation forms and iteratively refines its search based on symbolic execution results. This automated approach has the potential to dramatically accelerate mathematical exploration and discovery by reducing the time and effort required to identify and formalize mathematical relationships. The presented system demonstrates a viable pathway toward a more efficient and scalable method for uncovering mathematical identities from code.

title: Hierarchical Graph Embedding for Symbolic Reasoning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to symbolic reasoning using hierarchical graph embedding. The core idea is to construct a system that embeds graphs into a hierarchical structure, allowing for improved reasoning across the graph. We introduce a "graph-level abstraction" mechanism that decomposes the graph into subgraphs, each representing a level of abstraction. This decomposition enhances reasoning across the graph by facilitating the modeling of relationships between different levels of abstraction. The proposed system aims to overcome limitations in existing symbolic reasoning techniques by providing a more flexible and robust framework for representing and reasoning with complex symbolic structures. The system's design emphasizes the interplay between graph structure and abstraction levels, offering a promising path toward enhanced reasoning capabilities. This work addresses the challenge of efficiently representing and reasoning with large, interconnected graphs, particularly within the context of symbolic inference.

title: Quantum Walk Algorithms for Graph Partitioning
abstract: Graph partitioning is a crucial problem in computer science with applications in diverse areas like VLSI design, image segmentation, and network analysis. Traditional classical algorithms often face significant challenges when dealing with large and complex graphs, leading to increased computational time and memory requirements. This paper explores the potential of quantum walk algorithms to address this issue. We propose a framework for leveraging quantum walk algorithms to efficiently explore the connectivity structure of a graph and identify optimal partitions. The core idea involves mapping the graph's nodes and edges onto a quantum system and utilizing the inherent parallelism of quantum walks to traverse the graph. We present a theoretical analysis of the algorithm's potential speedup compared to classical approaches, focusing on scenarios where quantum computation offers a significant advantage. Specifically, we formulate the graph partitioning problem as a search problem on a graph represented as a quantum walk, considering the Hamiltonian operator and its eigenstates for efficient traversal. The effectiveness of the algorithm is dependent on the graph's structure and the ability to accurately simulate the quantum walk. The presented methodology provides a novel approach to graph partitioning, potentially leading to substantial performance improvements for large, complex graphs.

title: Quantum Decoherence-Based Algorithm Security Model
abstract: This paper presents a novel model for assessing algorithm security based on the principles of quantum decoherence. Current approaches to algorithm security often rely on classical computational assumptions, which may be vulnerable to future advancements in quantum computing. This model leverages the inherent vulnerability of quantum systems – decoherence – to provide a more robust and realistic security assessment. We construct a simulation environment that mimics a quantum computing scenario, allowing us to evaluate the resilience of algorithms against decoherence-induced errors. The model incorporates key concepts such as quantum gates, qubit states, and decoherence rates, represented mathematically as: * State of a qubit: |ψ⟩ = ∑i ci |i⟩ * Quantum gate operation: U = ∑i,j ci cj† |i⟩⟨j| * Decoherence rate: Γ (where Γ represents the probability of a qubit losing its quantum state per unit time) * Probability of error: Pe = exp(-Γt) , where t is the computation time. The core of the model is a simulation that propagates the state of a quantum system through a series of quantum gates, incorporating decoherence effects at each step. The model's output provides a quantifiable measure of an algorithm's security against decoherence, offering a valuable tool for designing and evaluating algorithms in the face of real-world quantum computing limitations. This approach moves beyond purely theoretical security assumptions and offers a more practically relevant framework for algorithm design and security analysis. ---

title: Qubits of a Feather, Flawed Together: A Comparative Analysis Review of Quantum Computing Architectures Compared
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Quantum Computing Architectures Compared in the context of Physics. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of quantum computing and qubits as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Physics.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Multi-Layer Parallel Neural Networks
abstract: This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement to enhance parallel computation and learning efficiency. Traditional neural networks are fundamentally limited by the speed of light and the sequential processing of information. We propose a multi-layer parallel neural network where neurons are interconnected through entangled qubits. The synaptic weights are encoded within the entangled states, and the activation function utilizes the superposition property of entangled states for parallel processing. A learning algorithm based on the interference effects within entangled states is developed to adjust the synaptic weights. This approach theoretically enables exponential increases in parallel computation capability and faster learning rates compared to conventional neural networks. The core claim of this work is that quantum entanglement provides a mechanism for instantaneous information transfer between neurons, surpassing the limitations of classical physics and significantly boosting neural network performance.

title: Neural Network-Based Symbolic Logic Reasoning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to symbolic logic reasoning by leveraging the capabilities of neural networks. The core idea is to train a neural network to learn the rules and patterns inherent in symbolic logic. This allows for the development of a system that can perform inference and judgment on new logical problems, effectively bridging the gap between traditional symbolic logic and the learning capabilities of artificial intelligence. We detail the architecture of the proposed neural network model, focusing on its ability to represent and apply logical rules. The system's performance is evaluated through a series of test cases designed to assess its accuracy and efficiency in solving logical problems. Ultimately, this work demonstrates a viable pathway for integrating symbolic reasoning with deep learning, potentially leading to more robust and adaptable reasoning systems.

title: Quantum-Inspired Probabilistic Programming for Complex System Simulation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to simulating complex systems using probabilistic programming, drawing inspiration from quantum mechanics. Traditional probabilistic programming methods often face challenges when dealing with high-dimensional systems due to the exponential growth of the probability space. We propose a framework that utilizes quantum-inspired superposition and interference techniques to represent and navigate this probability space more effectively. The core idea is to mimic the quantum ability to exist in multiple states simultaneously, thereby reducing the computational burden of exhaustive search. We demonstrate, theoretically and through a conceptual outline, how this approach could accelerate the simulation of systems with intricate dependencies. The method offers a potential pathway to overcome the limitations of classical probabilistic programming and provides a foundation for simulating complex scenarios with increased accuracy and speed. The key innovation lies in translating quantum principles – superposition and interference – into a probabilistic programming paradigm. This allows for a more efficient representation and exploration of complex probability distributions, leading to improved simulation performance. The paper outlines the necessary modifications to existing probabilistic programming languages to incorporate these quantum-inspired features. Further research will focus on developing a fully functional implementation and validating the approach with specific complex system models.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Boolean Logic – New Computational Paradigm
abstract: Quantum-enhanced Boolean logic represents a novel computational paradigm leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics, specifically superposition and entanglement, to achieve exponential speedups in computation. This paper proposes a design for a new Boolean logic system intrinsically linked to quantum circuits, aiming to exploit these phenomena for parallel processing and enhanced efficiency. We delve into the core mechanism of this system, exploring how quantum entanglement can be strategically employed to represent and manipulate Boolean logic operations. The exploration of this concept aims to push the boundaries of computational capabilities, offering a potential shift in the landscape of algorithmic design. The paper details the theoretical underpinnings, architectural considerations, and potential challenges associated with this approach.

title: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning with Intrinsic Motivation and Graph-Based Exploration
abstract: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (HRL) offers a promising approach to tackling complex sequential decision-making problems by decomposing them into smaller, manageable subtasks. However, traditional HRL methods often struggle with efficient exploration, frequently falling into local optima and failing to discover optimal policies. This paper introduces a novel framework that addresses these limitations by integrating intrinsic motivation with graph-based exploration strategies within a hierarchical reinforcement learning architecture. The core idea is to leverage a graph representation of the environment to drive intrinsic motivation, specifically novelty seeking and surprise, encouraging the agent to explore diverse and potentially rewarding states. We define the agent's internal representation as a graph where nodes represent states and edges represent transitions between them. The graph structure is dynamically updated based on the agent's experience, reflecting the environment's underlying complexity and offering a rich source of information for intrinsic motivation. The exploration strategy is then guided by this graph, prioritizing the exploration of nodes and transitions that are novel or surprising, leading to more efficient and robust learning. We present a detailed formulation of the HRL framework, including the key components and their interactions. The effectiveness of our approach is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and a comprehensive examination of the algorithm's performance. This work represents a significant advancement in HRL by providing a principled method for combining graph-based exploration and intrinsic motivation, resulting in improved exploration capabilities and enhanced learning efficiency.

title: A Perturbation Ladder for Sparse Autoencoder Dictionaries: Seed, Optimizer and Precision Against a Measured Baseline
abstract: Measures how much of a TopK sparse autoencoder's learned dictionary survives three perturbations - random seed, optimizer, and weight precision - using one matching procedure and one calibration so the three are comparable. Two autoencoders differing only in seed agree on 8.3-9.1% of matchable features (Pearson) across three pairwise comparisons at over 100x a permutation null. Against that baseline, changing the optimizer separates (intervals disjoint) while 4-bit quantisation does not (intervals overlap), so on this model and layer interpretability on quantised weights costs no more than the sampling variance of training a single autoencoder. Muon reaches equal-or-better reconstruction with 23x fewer dead features at 6.5x the wall clock, and dictionary collapse fires at the same step under both optimizers while only Muon recovers. All runs on a single Apple M1 Max.

Two autoencoders differing only in seed agree on 8.3-9.1% of matchable features (Pearson) across three pairwise comparisons at over 100x a permutation null. Against that baseline, changing the optimizer separates (intervals disjoint) while 4-bit quantisation does not (intervals overlap), so on this model and layer interpretability on quantised weights costs no more than the sampling variance of training a single autoencoder. Muon reaches equal-or-better reconstruction with 23x fewer dead features at 6.5x the wall clock, and dictionary collapse fires at the same step under both optimizers while only Muon recovers. All runs on a single Apple M1 Max.

title: AI-Driven Digital Twin Framework for Long-Term Photovoltaic Integration in Smart Cities: An Eleven-Year Comparative Study of Silicon Photovoltaic Technologies Under Semi-Arid Climate Conditions
abstract: The reliable long-term prediction of photovoltaic (PV) system performance is essential for optimizing operation, maintenance, and energy management in smart cities. Digital Twin (DT) technology has emerged as a promising approach for real-time monitoring and predictive analytics by continuously integrating physical system measurements with virtual models. However, many existing DT-based studies rely on limited validation periods, lack comprehensive uncertainty quantification, and provide insufficient comparisons with conventional forecasting approaches. To address these limitations, this study proposes a data-driven Digital Twin framework for daily photovoltaic energy production prediction for three silicon photovoltaic technologies (amorphous silicon, polycrystalline silicon, and monocrystalline silicon) operating under semi-arid climatic conditions in Morocco. The framework integrates data quality assessment and statistical production trend analysis based on linear regression, bootstrap confidence intervals, the Mann–Kendall trend test, and Sen’s slope estimator. In addition, the proposed DT model was benchmarked against persistence, linear regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models using a chronological training, validation, and independent testing framework. Model performance was evaluated over an independent test period of 602 consecutive days, representing approximately 1.65 years of continuous operation and more than one complete annual cycle. The proposed Digital Twin improved upon the standalone LightGBM model, achieving an RMSE of 1.3047 kWh/day, an MAE of 0.9255 kWh/day, a MAPE of 14.62%, and an R2 of 0.7015, compared with an RMSE of 1.3349 kWh/day, an MAE of 0.9637 kWh/day, and an R2 of 0.6875 for LightGBM. Over the 11-year monitoring period, the estimated long-term production trend rates were −0.566% yr−1 for a-Si, −0.335% yr−1 for pc-Si, and −0.260% yr−1 for mc-Si. Bootstrap analysis yielded median long-term production trend rates of −0.573, −0.326, and −0.251% yr−1, respectively, while Mann–Kendall tests indicated no statistically significant monotonic production trend for any technology (p = 0.1611, 0.2758, and 0.3502, respectively). The extended independent testing period, combined with statistical production trend analysis and comparative machine-learning evaluation, demonstrates the applicability of the proposed Digital Twin framework for photovoltaic performance monitoring and adaptive prediction under semi-arid climatic conditions.

title: Do Depressive Facial Patterns Transfer Across Cultures and Contexts? Evidence from a German RCT and E-DAIC
abstract: Automated assessment of depression from facial dynamics holds promise for scalable mental health monitoring, yet cross-corpus generalization of learned biomarkers remains an open challenge. We present a systematic bidirectional transfer study pairing the EmpkinS-EKSpression randomized controlled trial (RCT; N = 256, SCID-5-CV diagnoses) with the Extended Distress Analysis Interview Corpus (E-DAIC; N = 275, semi-structured clinical interviews), predicting depression severity and binary diagnostic status from facial action units, head pose, and gaze. Cross-corpus binary classification proves more robust than continuous PHQ-8 severity regression, with forward transfer achieving AUC = 0.70. Regression transfer is governed by functional context alignment: passive observation phases yield the most transferable models, while active emotion regulation phases elicit stronger within-corpus signals. These findings establish functional context alignment as the primary determinant of cross-corpus generalization, with passive elicitation contexts offering the best trade-off between within-corpus sensitivity and cross-corpus robustness.

title: ORB-SVM : An Innovative Hybrid Framework for Efficient Brain Tumor Detection from MRI Scans
abstract: Brain cancer remains one of the most significant challenges in modern medicine, where the accuracy of early stage diagnosis is a decisive factor in patient survival and treatment efficacy. Although Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is the established gold standard for visualizing neurological structures, the interpretation of these high dimensional scans is often complicated by subjective variability among practitioners and the inherent noise present in complex medical images. While contemporary approaches frequently rely on high parameter deep learning architectures, such models often involve significant computational costs and require extensive data for effective training. This study introduces a hybrid framework that utilizes the Oriented FAST and Rotated BRIEF (ORB) algorithm for precise feature extraction and a Support Vector Machine (SVM) for classification [1], [2]. The proposed approach achieves a sub- stantial data reduction of approximately 99.5%, which effectively minimizes the influence of non informative background data while preserving critical diagnostic patterns essential for tumor identification. By balancing feature sparsity with a robust kernel based classifier, this methodology addresses the limitations of over parameterized systems while maintaining high diagnostic integrity. Experimental evaluations conducted on the Br35H dataset demonstrate that the framework attains a classification accuracy of 97.5%. The findings suggest that the integration of localized feature representation and optimized classification provides a reliable and resource efficient alternative for medical image analysis, offering a structured solution that maintains per- formance without the need for extensive computational overhead.

title: Semantic Signal-Assisted Inspection and Recovery Allocation in Reverse Logistics
abstract: Reverse-logistics operators often decide how to inspect and route returned assets before their condition is fully observed, while full inspection consumes scarce labor. Semantic Signal-Assisted Decision Support converts return notes into a condition factor and a signal-quality score that guide inspection depth and recovery allocation under shared labor capacity. We evaluate the framework in three synthetic benchmark scenarios spanning information technology decommissioning, aircraft maintenance, and consumer-electronics returns. Across 30 paired simulation seeds, the keyword implementation improves net recovery value relative to a structured-feature comparator with noisy full inspection while reducing inspection cost in all three scenarios. A risk-blind comparator that skips inspection altogether still records higher value under the benchmark's purely economic objective. At matched inspection cost, score-guided targeting adds 53.9 thousand United States dollars per batch in the aircraft scenario but has little economic effect in the other two configurations; phrase and large language model extractors provide further gains in the aircraft scenario. These results show how narrative evidence can support inspection allocation before recovery decisions are made.

title: Bio-Information Quantum Entanglement
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum entanglement to revolutionize bio-information processing, specifically focusing on enhancing biological signal detection and decoding. Traditional methods in bioinformatics often rely on classical algorithms, which struggle to effectively capture and analyze subtle variations within complex biological systems. We propose a novel theoretical framework incorporating quantum entanglement, utilizing a specially designed quantum sensor to detect minute changes in biological signals. This approach offers a fundamentally new pathway for improving diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic efficacy. The core claim is that this quantum entanglement-based approach provides significantly enhanced sensitivity and precision compared to existing bio-information processing techniques. The research will investigate the principles of entanglement, its potential applications within biological systems, and the development of a prototype quantum sensor for real-world testing. This paper outlines the theoretical basis, proposed mechanism, and initial experimental considerations for this groundbreaking investigation.

title: Title: Topology-Enhanced Quantum Algorithm Verification
abstract: Quantum algorithms promise revolutionary advancements across diverse fields, yet their verification remains a significant challenge. Traditional verification methods often rely on exhaustive testing, which is computationally expensive and impractical for complex algorithms. This research proposes a novel approach leveraging topological concepts to proactively identify potential errors and vulnerabilities within quantum algorithms, significantly improving the accuracy and efficiency of the verification process. This work details the development of a method for analyzing the topological structure of quantum circuits, identifying anomalous regions indicative of errors, and ultimately providing a more robust verification framework. We introduce a novel topological analysis technique that incorporates the principles of graph theory and measure theory to effectively assess algorithm integrity. The core claim is that this method enhances the accuracy of quantum algorithm verification by detecting subtle errors that traditional approaches miss. This paper presents a comprehensive overview of the proposed method, including detailed mathematical formulations, illustrative examples, and a discussion of its potential impact on the future of quantum algorithm verification. The focus is on providing a practical, mathematically grounded solution to a critical problem within the quantum realm.

abstract: This paper investigates the intricate relationship between topology and quantum states, proposing a novel framework for modeling complex physical systems leveraging the inherent topological structure of quantum states. The core claim is that this framework offers a more accurate and efficient approach to describing these systems, particularly within the context of quantum computation. We detail the mechanism by which the underlying topological structure of quantum states informs the modeling process, aiming to provide a deeper understanding and improve the performance of quantum algorithms. This work explores the potential of utilizing topological data analysis (TDA) techniques to construct and interpret quantum states, thereby addressing limitations of traditional approaches.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Modeling and Simulating Complex Biological Systems
abstract: This paper proposes the use of probabilistic programming as a powerful tool for modeling and simulating complex biological systems. Current simulation methods frequently employ overly simplified assumptions, limiting their ability to accurately represent the inherent uncertainty present in biological processes. Probabilistic programming offers a framework for explicitly incorporating prior knowledge, rigorously quantifying uncertainty, and conducting sensitivity analysis, ultimately leading to more realistic and informative simulations. The core of this approach lies in leveraging the expressive power of probabilistic programming languages to define complex models where variables are represented as probability distributions, allowing for the simulation of systems under various conditions and the assessment of potential outcomes. This work outlines the key benefits, demonstrates the fundamental concepts, and highlights the potential impact of this methodology on various domains within biological research.

title: Title: Predictive Quantum Simulation with Wavefunction Collapse
abstract: Quantum simulation holds immense promise for understanding the fundamental laws of nature, particularly for complex systems where classical methods fail. However, the computational demands of simulating quantum systems are currently a significant barrier to their widespread application. This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum simulation – a predictive framework that leverages wavefunction collapse to dramatically reduce computational cost, enabling more efficient exploration of quantum phenomena. We detail a protocol for automatically collapsing wavefunction states as the simulation progresses, optimizing the simulation process and unlocking new possibilities for investigation. The core claim is that this design significantly accelerates the simulation of quantum systems without sacrificing accuracy. This work presents a rigorous analysis of the potential benefits of this approach, demonstrating its efficacy through simulations focusing on [mention a specific example, e.* the dynamics of a two-level quantum system]. The resulting framework has the potential to revolutionize quantum simulation, opening new avenues for scientific discovery.

title: Hierarchical Symbolic Regression with Bayesian Uncertainty
abstract: Symbolic regression (SR) offers a powerful approach to discovering mathematical relationships from data. However, its efficacy is often limited by the exponential growth of the search space, leading to brittle and unreliable expressions. This paper introduces a hierarchical symbolic regression algorithm incorporating Bayesian inference to mitigate these challenges. The system decomposes the regression problem into a hierarchy of subproblems, allowing for focused exploration. Bayesian methods are employed to quantify uncertainty at each stage, guiding the search towards more robust and generalizable expressions. This approach demonstrates improved scalability and reliability compared to standard SR methods, particularly when dealing with complex, high-dimensional systems. The core contribution lies in the integration of hierarchical decomposition with Bayesian uncertainty quantification for a more effective and stable discovery process.

title: Explainable Adversarial Generative Models
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to building explainable adversarial generative models. The core claim is to construct models capable of interpreting the process of generating adversarial samples, thereby enhancing the trustworthiness and security of generative models. The proposed mechanism integrates adversarial training with explainable AI techniques, specifically focusing on tracing the generation path of adversarial samples and analyzing the influential factors. Current generative models often operate as black boxes, making it difficult to understand how adversarial examples are created and how to defend against them. This work addresses this critical gap by providing a framework for understanding and mitigating the risks posed by adversarial attacks. The resulting models offer increased robustness and provide insights into vulnerabilities within the generative process. The primary objective is to move beyond simply detecting adversarial attacks to truly understanding *why* they succeed, ultimately leading to more secure and reliable generative models. The key contribution lies in the combined approach of adversarial training and explainable AI, offering a pathway toward more transparent and controllable generative systems.

title: Dynamic Programming for Reinforcement Learning with Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to reinforcement learning within Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes (POMDPs) utilizing dynamic programming techniques. Traditional reinforcement learning methods often struggle with the complexity and sample inefficiency inherent in POMDPs. Our proposed algorithm leverages dynamic programming's ability to systematically explore the state space while explicitly accounting for uncertainty, represented through a belief state. This belief state, a probability distribution over possible hidden states, guides the agent's decision-making process, leading to improved sample efficiency and faster convergence compared to standard reinforcement learning methods. The core of the algorithm involves a modified Bellman equation that incorporates the uncertainty represented by the belief state. We demonstrate, theoretically and conceptually, the advantages of this approach, outlining a framework suitable for tackling complex, partially observable environments. The key contributions lie in the integration of dynamic programming with belief state representation, offering a more targeted and effective learning strategy for POMDPs.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Program Synthesis via Temporal Logic Constraints
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neuro-symbolic program synthesis that leverages temporal logic constraints for rigorous verification. Traditional program synthesis methods frequently struggle to guarantee correctness when temporal relationships – such as ordering and timing – are involved. Our framework addresses this limitation by integrating temporal logic reasoning directly into the synthesis process. We propose a hybrid architecture comprising neural networks for pattern recognition and a temporal logic engine for verifying and refining synthesized programs against specified temporal requirements. The core innovation lies in providing a formal verification framework, significantly enhancing the reliability of neuro-symbolic program synthesis. We formalize this approach using mathematical notation, outlining the key components and their interactions. The resulting system demonstrates improved accuracy and reliability in generating programs that meet complex temporal constraints, representing a substantial advancement in the field. The proposed method tackles the challenge of temporal reasoning in program synthesis, offering a path towards more dependable and robust automated program generation.

title: Axiomatic Foundation for Explainable AI – Causal Inference as a Requirement
abstract: Current approaches to explainable AI (XAI) frequently fall short of providing genuinely understandable and trustworthy explanations. These methods often rely on post-hoc interpretations of black-box models, which can be misleading due to their failure to capture the underlying causal mechanisms driving predictions. This paper proposes a novel axiomatic foundation for XAI, arguing that true explanation necessitates a thorough understanding of causal relationships. We posit that causal inference represents a fundamental requirement for explainability, moving beyond superficial feature importance or local linear approximations. This framework introduces a rigorous approach to assessing explanations by evaluating their consistency with known causal structures, leading to more robust and reliable explanations. We define key concepts and provide a formal outline for evaluating explanation methods based on their ability to accurately represent and leverage causal knowledge. The core contribution is establishing a clear criterion – causal fidelity – for evaluating XAI methods, ensuring explanations reflect the true causal drivers of model behavior.

title: Simulating Evolution with Coupled Physical Systems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to optimization and search problems by integrating evolutionary algorithms with simulated physical systems. The core idea, termed "coupled physical systems," leverages the inherent constraints and dynamics of physical models to guide and refine the search process within evolutionary algorithms. Traditional evolutionary algorithms often suffer from issues such as premature convergence and sensitivity to initial populations. This work addresses these limitations by mapping the search space of the evolutionary algorithm onto a physically relevant system, such as a fluid dynamics simulation or a particle swarm optimization framework. title: 基于动态拓扑的机器学习模型评估
abstract: This paper presents a novel machine learning model evaluation framework based on dynamic topology, designed to assess model performance in complex environments. Traditional model evaluation methods rely on static models, limiting the potential for robust generalization. This framework leverages the inherent properties of dynamic topology to provide a more comprehensive and adaptive evaluation strategy, enhancing model robustness and generalization capabilities. We introduce a new method for dynamically characterizing model behavior within a complex, evolving landscape. This approach offers a shift towards a more nuanced and insightful assessment of model performance, particularly when dealing with data that exhibits significant structural changes or dependencies. The proposed framework focuses on quantifying the model's ability to adapt and maintain its performance across diverse conditions. The core mechanism involves the construction of a dynamic topology representation of the model's output space, enabling the identification of critical regions and vulnerabilities. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of carefully selected experiments, showcasing its ability to outperform traditional methods in evaluating models with varying levels of complexity and uncertainty. The results highlight the significant potential of dynamic topology in improving model reliability and adaptability.

title: Graph Generative Adversarial Networks for Knowledge Graph Completion
abstract: Knowledge graphs (KGs) are increasingly used to represent and reason about complex information. A significant challenge in KG management is incompleteness, where many potential relationships between entities remain unobserved. Traditional KG completion methods often rely on statistical inference or embedding techniques, which may struggle to capture complex relational patterns. This paper proposes a novel approach utilizing Graph Generative Adversarial Networks (GANS) to address this challenge. We introduce a generator network that generates new triples (si, rj, ok) and a discriminator network that assesses the likelihood of these generated triples based on the existing KG structure. The generator and discriminator engage in an adversarial training process, where the generator attempts to produce realistic triples that fool the discriminator, while the discriminator strives to distinguish between real and generated triples. Our approach leverages the GAN framework to learn complex relational patterns and enhance the completeness of the KG. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method through theoretical analysis and outline potential future directions. The key contribution lies in applying GANs to the inherently relational problem of KG completion, offering a potentially more powerful and flexible solution compared to existing techniques.

title: Fabrication on absent fields: a pre-registered six-arm document-extraction bake-off (round 1)
abstract: Complete public artifact of a pre-registered document-extraction bake-off: six extraction setups (Velrim’s included — Velrim ran the comparison and sells one of the six) over 124 real documents, scored under an analysis plan frozen and published before the first paid call. Headline measurement: fabrication on absent fields — pooled across the six setups, 17% of the fields absent from the document came back with an invented value. The archive holds the frozen analysis plan, golden sets and probe set, every raw per-field output with request IDs, per-repeat scores, figures, the disclosure register, and the scoring CLI (velrim-eval); re-scoring the published outputs needs no keys and costs nothing. Code is Apache-2.0; source corpora carry their own licenses (CC BY 4.0 / MIT), attributed in the archive. Write-up: velrim.com/research/fabrication-on-absent-fields — living repository: github.com/velrimhq/velrim-eval.

title: Robust UAV Detection and Classification in Noisy RF Environments via Multimodal CNN-Based IQ and Spectrogram Fusion
abstract: This study aims to autonomously detect and classify Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), which are becoming increasingly widespread, based on their emitted radio frequency (RF) signals in highly noisy and interference-prone RF environments where traditional optical and radar-based methods prove insufficient. The dataset used in this study is the “Noisy Drone RF Signal Classification” dataset, which consists of seven classes in total—six different drone models and one noise class—and is balanced across classes. As the methodological approach, a multimodal hybrid deep learning (DL) architecture was developed, integrating raw time-domain IQ signals (1D-CNN) with frequency-domain spectrogram representations (2D-CNN). To enhance model performance and generalization capability, techniques such as Batch Normalization, Dropout, Label Smoothing, and Gradient Clipping were incorporated into the architecture. The model was trained using the AdamW optimization algorithm alongside a cosine annealing learning rate scheduler. In order to efficiently process large-scale datasets, memory management optimizations including memory-mapped files (mmap) and lazy loading were implemented. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed multimodal model achieves an accuracy of 87.42% and an F1-score of 0.87, indicating strong detection performance. SNR-based analyses reveal that the model achieves accuracy levels ranging between 64.52% and 82.40% under negative-SNR conditions (−20 to 0 dB), while exceeding 89% accuracy under positive-SNR conditions. The findings indicate that multimodal DL approaches can achieve high performance in UAV detection and classification even in noisy RF environments.

title: Social federated learning (SFL): Leveraging shared data to boost learning performance
abstract: Collaboration between edge devices has the potential to scale up machine learning (ML) by enabling access to unprecedented amounts of data. Federated learning (FL) is a collaborative algorithm in which clients learn from each other without sharing private data. However, edge devices tend to have different data distributions because they are naturally exposed to different data sources. This heterogeneity, also known as non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data, has been shown to decrease the accuracy of FL. We study how limited data sharing among users can alleviate this performance degradation. Such sharing can occur naturally on a social graph or be incentivized by the platform. We evaluated the performance gains of data sharing on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 across topologies including complete graphs, clusters, and stochastic block models. We empirically demonstrate that modest data sharing between neighbors on a social graph enhances learning performance in the non-IID case. Interestingly, we found that data sharing could also improve performance in the IID case. By normalizing the dataset sizes, we verified that this boost is significant even if sharing does not increase the number of data points per client. Therefore, data sharing is an efficient technique for improving social federated learning (SFL).

title: SecDT: A Profile-Based Security Layer for TRDP Communications
abstract: The Train Real-time Data Protocol (TRDP) is widely used on rolling stock but it provides limited native support for cryptographic protection. Furthermore, the multicast traffic profile used in TRDP Process Data to exchange critical information between onboard subsystems makes the introduction of cryptographic protection a challenge. This paper presents a lightweight security layer for secure TRDP communication that implements a number of security profiles built around modern cryptographic algorithms. This additional layer relies on an On-board Key Management System (OKMS) for both security profile negotiation, dynamic key distribution and key lifecycle management. The security profiles allow for cryptographic agility and flexibility, ranging from simple authentication to Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD) algorithms. The security profile negotiation procedure guarantees all TRDP End Devices (ED) on a common Communication ID (ComID) share the same security profile and can therefore process each other's messages. A prototype implementation based on mbedTLS and Arm Platform Security Architecture (PSA) was developed and evaluated. Experimental results demonstrate manageable overhead, suitable for the real-time and time-sensitive communication found on rolling stock.

title: Competitive Market Behavior of LLMs
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as economic agents, yet there is little evidence whether LLM agents are suited for participating in market mechanisms designed for humans, and whether these mechanisms deliver desired outcomes when faced with LLM agents. We address this question by replicating seminal economic experiments, replacing human subjects with LLM agents. We place agents in a double auction environment, which is a widely-used market mechanism. We check whether such a market is able to deliver an efficient allocation of resources, thereby testing a novel dimension of alignment of LLM agents -- their compatibility with a fundamental market mechanism. We find that markets populated by LLM agents exhibit slower or no convergence towards market equilibrium, thus providing less efficient allocations than markets populated by humans. We then analyze agents' individual trading decisions and find substantial heterogeneity both across model families and market roles. We also run a lexical analysis of Chain-of-Thought (CoT) traces generated by the agents. We find that the decision to execute a trade rather than continue incrementally adjusting prices is associated with a shift from strategic considerations toward urgency. We publicly release our testing framework, which can be used for future evaluations.

title: New binary optimal LCD codes using heuristic embedding
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the construction of binary optimal LCD codes through short LCD embeddings. For this purpose, we design heuristic frameworks based on a greedy algorithm. We explore the search spaces of LCD embeddings using the fact that an invertible matrix together with an arbitrary matrix yields an LCD embedding. We therefore use elementary row operations on the invertible block and single entry-flips on the arbitrary block as local moves in a greedy algorithm. Using this method, we have found $14$ optimal new LCD codes with dimensions 7 and 8 for lengths from 55 to 201.

title: FlatLands: Generative Floormap Completion From a Single Egocentric View
abstract: A single egocentric image typically captures only a small portion of the floor, yet a complete metric traversability map of the surroundings would better serve applications such as indoor navigation. We introduce FlatLands, a dataset and benchmark for single-view bird's-eye view (BEV) floor completion. The dataset contains 270,575 observations from 17,656 real metric indoor scenes drawn from six existing datasets, with aligned observation, visibility, validity, and ground-truth BEV maps, and the benchmark includes both in- and out-of-distribution evaluation protocols. We compare training-free approaches, deterministic models, ensembles, and stochastic generative models. Finally, we instantiate the task as an end-to-end monocular RGB-to-floormaps pipeline. FlatLands provides a rigorous testbed for uncertainty-aware indoor mapping and generative completion for embodied navigation.

title: Masking a Field's Loss Does Not Isolate That Field
abstract: Masking a field's loss does not isolate that field. Five LoRA runs on a 0.6B guard model. Runs 1-2 show a masked output field moving anyway. Runs 3-5 add a three-arm target-module ablation: attention-only and MLP-only are disjoint and each independently destroys the model's third severity class, so retargeting the adapter is not available as a repair. A documented operator control becomes a silent no-op.

title: Information Entropy Calculation & Quantum Topology
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum topology to information entropy calculation, presenting a novel algorithm that leverages this structure for enhanced computational efficiency. We propose a quantum computation framework centered around "information encoding-decoding," aiming to significantly improve compression and communication strategies. The core mechanism centers around utilizing quantum topological properties to build a more efficient and robust system for information processing. The paper details the algorithm's design, the theoretical underpinnings of the quantum topology approach, and preliminary results demonstrating potential improvements over existing methods. The investigation considers the implications of this approach for understanding fundamental information theory and its applications in data compression and secure communication.

title: Dynamic Entropy-Based Machine Learning Model (DEBM)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning model, the Dynamic Entropy-Based Machine Learning Model (DEBM), that leverages the concept of entropy to dynamically adjust model parameters and enhance its adaptability to changing data. Traditional machine learning models often rely on static parameters, limiting their ability to effectively learn from evolving datasets. The DEBM addresses this limitation by incorporating an entropy-based mechanism that continuously monitors and adjusts model parameters based on data fluctuations, resulting in a more robust and adaptive learning process. The paper details the model's architecture, the entropy-driven adjustment process, and its potential applications across various machine learning domains. We present preliminary results demonstrating the model's effectiveness in handling complex data patterns and achieving superior performance compared to traditional approaches.

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization of Neural Network Weight Initialization
abstract: Traditional methods for initializing weights in neural networks, such as Xavier and He initialization, rely on statistical assumptions about the distribution of network activations. These assumptions often fail to capture the complex dynamics of deep learning, leading to suboptimal performance and slower convergence. This paper proposes a novel approach to neural network weight initialization inspired by quantum mechanics. We leverage concepts like superposition and tunneling to explore a wider range of potential weight values, effectively broadening the search space for the optimal initialization. The core idea is to treat the weight initialization problem as a quantum exploration process, where weights are represented as quantum states and the optimization process involves manipulating these states. We introduce a mathematical framework based on probability amplitudes and phase functions to model this quantum exploration. The proposed method, termed Quantum-Inspired Neural Network Initialization (QINNI), aims to significantly improve the initial state of the network, leading to faster convergence and better overall performance. The effectiveness of QINNI is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and simulations, showcasing its potential to overcome the limitations of conventional weight initialization strategies.

abstract: Quantum Topologies, a novel approach to quantum computing, offers a unique framework for algorithm optimization. title: Causal Discovery from Interventional and Observational Data using Bayesian Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of integrating interventional and observational data to enhance the accuracy and robustness of causal discovery algorithms. Traditional causal discovery methods often rely solely on observational data, which may be biased due to confounding variables or unobserved confounders. This research proposes a novel approach by leveraging Bayesian networks, allowing for the explicit modeling of causal relationships derived from both experimental (interventional) and observational data. The core claim is that combining these data sources can significantly improve the identification of true causal structures. The mechanism involves utilizing Bayesian networks to represent the probabilistic dependencies between variables, incorporating interventions to directly measure causal effects alongside observational measurements. We explore the theoretical underpinnings and discuss the potential benefits and challenges of this integrated approach, highlighting its advantages over existing techniques. We demonstrate that incorporating interventional data can resolve ambiguities and improve the accuracy of discovered causal graphs, particularly in scenarios with complex confounding. The primary contribution of this work is a framework for robust causal discovery that accounts for both the strength and direction of causal influences.

title: Artificial Intelligent (AI) and Endangered Language Preservation: Challenges Among Igbo, Hausa and Yoruba
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligent (AI) is geared recently into a diverse array of innovative tools that empowered linguistic communities to document, preserve, and share endangered languages. Considering the inherent complexities of linguistics, technical limitations, and ethical consideration on human system as an assessing long-term sustainability of language preservation, a focus on AI-driven tools in preserving endangered language rears. This study specifically aims to explore AI preservative potentials in preserving endangered languages specifically the cultural and linguistic subtleties, such as nuances of expression and idiomatic phrases, that define endangered languages among the three major ethnics languages in Nigeria. To systematically draw strings of inferences on that, a cross-sectional research design and quota sampling technique was adopted. 45 married men and women (15 each) from the 3 major ethnic group (Igbo, Hausa, and Yoruba) in Nigeria were sampled using structured questionnaire. title: Self-Adaptive Topology of Quantum Entanglement Analysis
abstract: This paper investigates the application of self-adaptive topology to quantum entanglement analysis, aiming to refine the measurement process and improve the accuracy of entanglement characterization. Traditional approaches often rely on static models, limiting the ability to dynamically adjust the analysis based on the system's state. We propose a novel method that leverages the inherent properties of self-adaptive topology to enhance entanglement analysis. The core mechanism focuses on dynamically modifying the topology during the entanglement measurement, thereby minimizing noise and maximizing the fidelity of the measurement. The resulting system exhibits improved performance in analyzing complex entangled states, demonstrating a significant advancement in the precision of quantum entanglement characterization.

title: Adaptive-Adaptive Bayesian Modeling
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive-adaptive Bayesian modeling framework designed to enhance predictive accuracy and generalization capabilities. Traditional model parameterization methods often struggle to adapt to evolving data patterns, leading to suboptimal performance. Our approach leverages an adaptive learning algorithm that dynamically adjusts model parameters based on data, minimizing overfitting and maximizing predictive effectiveness. We present a novel methodology incorporating Bayesian inference and adaptive parameter updates, demonstrating significant improvements in prediction consistency and robustness across a range of datasets. The core mechanism centers on a hierarchical Bayesian model, allowing for flexible representation of uncertainty and enabling more informed parameter selection. This work addresses a critical challenge in machine learning by providing a robust and adaptable solution for complex data analysis.

title: Quantum State Dynamics: A Novel Modeling Approach for Enhanced Computational Precision
abstract: Quantum state dynamics represents a paradigm shift in the field of quantum information processing, offering unprecedented control over quantum systems. This paper explores a novel modeling approach, leveraging dynamic topology transformations, to enhance the precision of quantum state representations. We introduce a framework wherein the inherent topology of a quantum state is continuously adjusted through a series of transformations, allowing for a more accurate representation of the system's behavior. This approach overcomes limitations of static models by dynamically adapting to complex quantum environments. The core mechanism focuses on the iterative adjustment of topology, achieving a significant improvement in computational fidelity compared to traditional methods. The results demonstrate the efficacy of this methodology in modeling various quantum systems, highlighting its potential for advancing quantum algorithm design and error mitigation.

title: Core Claim: Developing a quantum topological vulnerability assessment method, leveraging quantum state topology to evaluate the vulnerability of quantum systems to quantum attacks, and discovering quantum security strategies.
abstract: Quantum computing has rapidly advanced, presenting both immense opportunities and significant challenges. Quantum attacks, exploiting vulnerabilities in quantum systems, pose a serious threat to current cryptographic protocols and essential technologies. Current vulnerability assessment methods are largely based on classical algorithms, often lacking the ability to accurately predict and mitigate these attacks. This research introduces a novel quantum topological vulnerability assessment framework, utilizing quantum state topology to comprehensively evaluate the susceptibility of quantum systems to various attacks. The framework employs a sophisticated approach that exploits the inherent topological properties of quantum states to identify and quantify potential weaknesses. The core of the method involves constructing a quantum state representation that encodes the system's topology and dynamically assesses this representation to identify vulnerabilities. This assessment is then compared against known attack scenarios, leading to the discovery of quantum security strategies. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this framework through simulations and preliminary experimental results, highlighting its potential to significantly improve the robustness of quantum systems. This work presents a fundamentally new approach to quantum security evaluation, offering a more precise and adaptable method compared to existing techniques.

title: Quantum Back-Erasing Reconstruction and Control
abstract: This paper investigates the reconstruction and control of quantum decoherence through a novel approach of inverse back-erasure. Traditional decoherence control strategies primarily focus on mitigating the effects of environmental noise, often employing passive shielding or error correction techniques. This work proposes a proactive method utilizing feedback control to actively reverse the decoherence process, thereby enhancing the coherence of quantum states. The core concept involves precisely measuring the quantum system's interaction with its environment and applying corrective actions to counteract the detrimental effects of decoherence. We explore theoretical frameworks based on Hamiltonian engineering and feedback control theory, formulating a mathematical model for the system and outlining the control strategy. The central equation governing the process is: Δψ(t+Δt) = α(t) Δψ(t) + β(t) (H - η(t) ⋅ H') Δψ(t) where Δψ(t+Δt) is the quantum state at time t+Δt, α(t) is the decoherence factor, β(t) is the control factor, H is the Hamiltonian of the system, H' is the environmental Hamiltonian, and η(t) is the feedback control term. The goal is to manipulate β(t) and η(t) to minimize the effect of decoherence. The effectiveness of this approach is discussed in terms of coherence time extension and entanglement preservation. The research contributes a new paradigm for quantum control, offering potential advancements in quantum computing, quantum communication, and quantum sensing. ---

title: Quantum Mechanics Principle-Based Parallel Computing Architecture
abstract: This paper proposes a novel parallel computing architecture grounded in the principles of quantum mechanics. The core concept involves leveraging quantum phenomena like superposition and entanglement to construct a quantum bit (qubit)-based parallel computing system, thereby facilitating the concurrent execution of complex computational tasks. The architecture aims to significantly enhance computational efficiency compared to classical parallel computing approaches. This document outlines the theoretical framework, key architectural components, and potential operational principles of this system. It explores the challenges and opportunities presented by implementing such a system and highlights the potential for transformative advancements in fields reliant on computationally intensive tasks, such as drug discovery, materials science, and artificial intelligence.

title: Symbolic Simulation of Complex Systems using Neural Networks
abstract: The increasing complexity of real-world systems – ranging from financial markets to biological networks – poses a significant challenge to traditional simulation methods. Conventional simulation techniques, such as differential equations and agent-based modeling, often struggle to capture the emergent behavior arising from intricate interactions. Neural networks offer a promising alternative due to their ability to learn complex patterns from data. However, their inherent "black-box" nature limits their utility in systems requiring interpretability, transparency, and precise control. This paper proposes a novel hybrid approach to complex system simulation, integrating neural networks with symbolic simulation. The core idea is to utilize a neural network to approximate the dynamics of the system, while simultaneously maintaining a symbolic representation for understanding and controlling the simulation. This hybrid approach aims to combine the predictive power of neural networks with the interpretability and controllability of symbolic models. The specific formulation involves a neural network trained to predict the state of the system at a given time, based on its current state and input parameters. The output of the neural network is then used to update the symbolic representation, and vice-versa, creating a feedback loop that allows for continuous refinement and adaptation. This process is facilitated by carefully designed loss functions that balance prediction accuracy with symbolic representation fidelity. The paper outlines the key components of this hybrid system and discusses its potential applications across various domains.

title: Multi-Layer Controlled Multi-Output Remote State Preparation of Single-Particle States
abstract: We propose two multi-layer controlled multi-output remote state preparation (RSP) schemes for arbitrary single-qubit and single-qudit states. Twelve-particle entangled channels are constructed in two-dimensional and d-dimensional Hilbert spaces, and a hierarchical authorization mechanism is introduced to enable controllers with different permission levels to jointly and selectively regulate the reconstruction of quantum states at multiple receivers. First, based on a twelve-qubit maximally entangled channel, we design a deterministic three-layer controlled multi-output RSP protocol in which one sender assists three receivers in preparing their respective target single-qubit states. In this protocol, the controllers are assigned high-, medium-, and low-level permissions. Under different multi-layer control conditions, the three receivers can reconstruct their respective original single-qubit states by performing appropriate local unitary operations. The results show that the protocol achieves unit success probability, exhibits good universality and provides a structured basis for extension to larger multi-user settings, and enforces hierarchical access control by preventing unauthorized receivers from deterministically reconstructing the target states. Subsequently, we replace the maximally entangled channel with a non-maximally entangled twelve-qubit state. After the sender performs two specific three-qubit projective measurements, the receivers can probabilistically reconstruct their respective target states under the same three-layer control structure by introducing auxiliary qubits, applying controlled-U gates, and measuring the auxiliary systems. Finally, by employing positive operator-valued measurements, the above scheme is generalized from qubit systems to arbitrary d-dimensional qudit systems, providing a theoretical basis for exploring larger multi-user quantum communication settings with hierarchical authorization.
