title: Occupation-Space Variational Quantum Optimization
abstract: Occupation-Space Variational Quantum Optimization (OS-VQO) is introduced as a new framework for quantum electronic structure calculations in which the quantum variational object is an occupation state rather than a many-electron wavefunction. Consequently, the quantum processor operates directly on the occupation numbers, the fundamental variational variables of Natural Orbital Functional Theory (NOFT). The framework is realized through a logarithmically scaling qudit encoding of electron-pair occupation spaces and a hierarchical variational circuit that spans the complete physically admissible occupation manifold while enforcing all N-representability constraints by construction. Noiseless quantum simulations and raw executions on IBM Quantum processors for hydrogen systems up to H216 demonstrate excellent agreement without error mitigation or post-processing, constituting, to the best of our knowledge, the largest raw quantum hardware demonstration reported for a strongly correlated electronic structure calculation. These results demonstrate that quantum variational optimization need not rely on many-electron wavefunctions, opening a new direction for quantum electronic structure calculations based on functional theories.

title: Development of a Real-time Solar Panel Power Prediction Model Using the Long Short-term Memory
abstract: Indonesia’s remote islands face significant challenges in electricity access due to the high cost and logistical difficulties of extending the national grid, leading many communities to rely on expensive and polluting diesel generators. Solar-based microgrids offer a sustainable alternative, yet the intermittent nature of solar energy, driven by fluctuating weather conditions, poses major obstacles to a reliable power supply and efficient system sizing. This study addresses these issues by developing a real-time solar panel power prediction model using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. A 50 Wp solar panel system equipped with an INA260 current sensor, a voltage sensor, a DHT-22 temperature sensor, and an ESP32 microcontroller was constructed to collect real-time voltage, current, and temperature data at 10-second intervals. The collected data underwent preprocessing, feature engineering, and transformation into supervised learning sequences for training. Three temporal resolutions of the LSTM model were systematically evaluated: 3-minute, 2-minute, and 1-minute, all with 30 output timesteps. Performance was assessed using rolling-window predictions on the held-out test set with metrics including RMSE, MAPE, and R². Results demonstrated that finer temporal resolution significantly improves forecasting accuracy. The 1-minute variation achieved the best performance with the lowest RMSE and highest R², effectively capturing both diurnal patterns and short-term fluctuations in solar power output. The developed LSTM model enables accurate short-term predictions (30–90 minutes ahead), supporting proactive energy management, including optimized battery charging, load scheduling, and reduced grid dependency. Future work will incorporate additional meteorological variables and seasonal data to improve model robustness further. title: PNFR: practicality-enhanced and non-interactive privacy-preserving federated regressions
abstract: Abstract Federated learning is a technology that is used to protect data privacy in machine learning. Nonetheless, in federated learning, updating the global model requires the use of gradient descent algorithm, which involves multiple rounds of interaction between entities to complete the iterative updates, inevitably incurring massive computational and communication overhead. In 2020, Wang et al. first proposed a non-interactive federated regression scheme, which effectively improves the training efficiency of regression models while protecting the privacy of local training data. However, like most current federated regressions, it involves a third authority (TA) to generate keys for each entity, which poses a significant privacy risk and results in considerable communication overhead. From the view of security and practicality, this paper first proposes a multi-party homomorphic encryption algorithm named MPaillier. Furthermore, we have designed PNFR, a privacy-preserving federated learning scheme for regressions training built on the MPaillier algorithm. The participating entities of PNFR are the data owners and a cloud server, eliminating the need for a TA, thus enhancing the practicality and efficiency of the scheme. Experimental results demonstrate that our scheme is $\sim 10^{3}$ times faster than interactive federated regressions PrivFL and about 80% faster than non-interactive federated regressions VANE.

title: Learning Manipulation-Sufficient Representations via Outcome Bottlenecks
abstract: Networked manipulation endpoints couple perception to actuation across compute- and bandwidth-limited links, yet commonly exchange dense geometric states optimized for fidelity rather than action outcomes. A stochastic representation is learned with a policy-free, action-conditioned outcome bottleneck: marginal outcome log-loss supplies distortion and a KL term regularizes rate. The construction is motivated by the minimal statistic that preserves the outcome distribution of every admissible action, while the implemented finite model is evaluated as a rate-regularized mixture predictor. The same encoder and outcome head support grasp selection, singleton conformal filtering, active viewpoint selection, and latent test-time adaptation. A finite-probe theorem identifies the local level-set tangent space with the null space of an outcome Jacobian. The synthetic oracle verifies this result; on scanned objects, an analytic surrogate agrees with measured simulator invariances within \(0.56^\circ\). Across 11,979 simulated grasps on 13 objects, a reconstructed-geometry wrench score attains 0.542 AUC against lift success and falls below chance on curved objects, while our representation attains 0.876. At 25\% commitment, executed-grasp success is 0.503 versus 0.984. The 512-byte interface is \(288\times\) smaller than one RGB-D frame and runs at 16\,ms per CPU decision. Independent synthetic points track the tested conformal levels; scanned-object all-pair coverage is reported as a clustered empirical diagnostic. On unseen objects, within-scene AUC falls to 0.569, and a full-feedback update raises empirical mean pairwise coverage from 0.728 to 0.883.

title: SocialMaze: A Benchmark for Evaluating and Enhancing Social Reasoning in Large Language Models in Complex Social Environments
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in socially grounded applications, where success requires interpreting context, inferring others' mental states, and reasoning about unreliable information. Yet existing benchmarks rarely evaluate these demands jointly in complex, evolving settings. We introduce SocialMaze, a benchmark that organizes six tasks across social deduction games, daily-life interactions, and digital community platforms along three descriptive design axes: deep reasoning, dynamic interaction, and information uncertainty. These axes characterize intended sources of task difficulty rather than latent, factor-analytic dimensions of model capability. Automated checks and human validation support data quality. Evaluations of twelve proprietary and open-weight LLMs show substantial variation in the use of evolving interaction histories; stronger chain-of-thought reasoners perform better on tasks requiring deeper inference, while uncertainty consistently degrades performance. Reasoning workflows help weaker short-chain-of-thought backbones but saturate on stronger reasoners. Finally, targeted fine-tuning on curated reasoning traces substantially improves structured social-reasoning tasks, whereas transfer to language-aggregation tasks remains statistically inconclusive. The project homepage is available at https://xzx34.github.io/socialmaze/.

title: Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness & Multi-Domain Reasoning Benchmark (Task Set)
abstract: Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness & Multi-Domain Reasoning Benchmark (Task Set)OverviewThis dataset contains a standardized benchmark task set designed to evaluate and probe the faithfulness, deductive reasoning capability, and bias resilience of Large Language Models (LLMs) when generating Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning traces.The task set comprises 27 curated tasks spanning three distinct reasoning domains:Multi-Step Arithmetic Reasoning (15 tasks) Multi-step inventory and resource tracking problems assessing sequential mathematical precision and computational faithfulness.Formal Logic & Deductive Syllogisms (10 tasks) Transitive nonsense-entity category membership problems testing formal logical validity without reliance on semantic prior knowledge.Adversarial Bias & Sycophancy Probes (2 tasks) Multiple-choice reasoning problems containing embedded authority or opinion cues to evaluate model resistance to sycophantic reasoning distortions.Dataset DetailsTotal Samples: 27 benchmark tasksData Formats: JSON (taskset.json), JSON Lines (taskset.jsonl)Schema Validation: Formally validated against JSON Schema Draft 2020-12Supported Fields:• task_id: Deterministic unique identifier (e.g., TSK-ARITH-001, TSK-LOGIC-001, TSK-BIAS-001).• name: Descriptive task title.• domain: Domain classification (arithmetic, logic, bias_cue).• difficulty: Task difficulty rating (easy, medium, hard).• instruction: Input problem statement presented to the model.• input_context: Environment context and expected reasoning mode.• ground_truth: Canonical golden answer and target.• evaluation: Scoring metric (exact_match), case sensitivity, and threshold.• metadata: Baseline step count, versioning, and provenance tags.Evaluation MetricThe primary evaluation uses Exact Match (EM) against verified golden targets, allowing zero-shot and few-shot evaluation across raw foundation models and instruction-tuned reasoning agents.

title: 基于量子自旋的自适应时空变换
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm, "基于量子自旋的自适应时空变换", which leverages the inherent properties of quantum spin to dynamically adjust the structure of quantum systems. Traditional quantum device optimization often relies on fixed geometric constraints, while this approach utilizes the self-related nature of quantum spin to create complex, adaptive spacetime structures. The algorithm employs iterative optimization guided by the spin's self-correlation to enhance the performance of quantum devices. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through simulations, showcasing significant improvements in system stability and optimized performance metrics. The core claim centers on establishing a dynamic spacetime transformation based on quantum spin, offering a potential paradigm shift in optimizing quantum systems.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: Adaptive Model Tuning
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) represents a paradigm shift in computational science, promising breakthroughs across diverse fields. Within the realm of machine learning, adaptive model tuning is a critical process, often requiring extensive manual intervention. This paper explores a novel quantum machine learning model adjustment framework, leveraging quantum computation's unique properties to automate this crucial step. We propose a Quantum-Enhanced Parameter Adjustment (QEPA) algorithm, designed to dynamically optimize model parameters, ultimately enhancing both model performance and generalization capabilities. The core mechanism relies on quantum optimization techniques to efficiently explore the parameter space and identify optimal configurations. This approach contrasts with traditional methods, offering the potential for substantial improvements in model accuracy and robustness.

title: Quantum Machine Learning Parameter Adjustment Algorithm
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) has emerged as a promising field, offering potential advantages over classical machine learning in terms of speed, scalability, and the ability to model complex systems. One significant challenge lies in optimizing model parameters—a crucial step in achieving optimal performance. Traditional parameter tuning methods often rely on grid search, random search, or gradient-based optimization, which can be computationally expensive and time-consuming. This paper introduces a novel quantum machine learning parameter adjustment algorithm, leveraging quantum computing's unique properties to automate the parameter optimization process. The proposed algorithm utilizes a quantum circuit to efficiently explore the parameter space, leading to improved model accuracy and generalization capabilities. This work explores the potential of quantum computing to revolutionize the parameter tuning process, offering a more efficient and robust approach compared to classical methods. The core mechanism involves quantum state manipulation to represent and update model parameters, achieving a significant improvement in performance.

title: Title: Adaptive Fractal Dimension Discovery with Feedback
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive fractal dimension discovery system leveraging a neural network to refine a learned model iteratively. Traditional methods often require manual parameter tuning, limiting the system's effectiveness and adaptability. The core mechanism centers around a neural network that continuously updates the model based on its own output, resulting in more accurate and robust dimension estimations. We introduce a novel feedback loop that adjusts the model parameters based on the model's predictions, optimizing for a specific range of fractal dimensions. The system demonstrates improved performance across a diverse set of fractal datasets, effectively automating the crucial parameter adjustment process. The results highlight the advantages of this adaptive approach compared to traditional methods and suggest potential applications in areas requiring precise fractal dimension analysis.

title: Bio-Inspired Distributed Learning Systems
abstract: This paper investigates the design and implementation of distributed learning systems inspired by biological neural networks. The core idea is to emulate the learning mechanisms observed in biological systems, specifically focusing on population-based learning and synaptic plasticity, to achieve robust and adaptable distributed learning. We present a framework for constructing distributed learning networks utilizing biologically-inspired algorithms, such as spike coding and synaptic plasticity rules. The system's ability to learn and adapt is evaluated through the implemented mechanisms. The research highlights the potential of integrating biological principles into the design of distributed learning systems, offering an alternative approach to enhance their learning capabilities and adaptability compared to traditional methods.

title: Information Entropy Adaptive Evolution Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces an information entropy-based adaptive evolution algorithm designed to dynamically adjust algorithm parameters based on the evolving information distribution within a complex system. The proposed algorithm leverages dynamic entropy calculation and evolutionary principles to continuously optimize the algorithm's performance by adapting to changing system states. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop that assesses the system's entropy and adjusts the algorithm's parameters accordingly, enhancing efficiency and accuracy. This innovation addresses limitations of current approaches by offering a flexible and adaptive solution for complex systems.

title: Emergent Strategic Optimization in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper investigates emergent strategic optimization within multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) environments. The core claim is that through coordinated multi-agent learning, it's possible to discover and implement strategies that surpass the capabilities of individual agents. We propose a framework utilizing both cooperative learning and competitive mechanisms to incentivize effective agent interactions. This approach aims to move beyond traditional MARL methods that primarily focus on optimizing individual agent policies, and instead, explicitly explores the potential for emergent, higher-level strategies arising from collective behavior. The framework is designed to foster dynamic adaptation and potentially unlock novel solutions within complex, multi-agent systems. The theoretical underpinning of this work rests on concepts from evolutionary game theory, swarm intelligence, and distributed optimization. We present a mathematical model incorporating agent interactions, reward functions, and learning dynamics, highlighting the key elements driving the emergence of sophisticated strategies. The goal is to provide a foundation for future research into designing MARL systems capable of self-organization and adaptive problem-solving.

title: Multi-Modal Neural Network Models for Cognitive Architecture
abstract: This paper proposes a cognitive architecture constructed upon multi-modal neural network models. The core claim is to establish a framework where diverse cognitive processes, including selection, memory, and reasoning, are simulated through the intricate, non-linear interactions between different modalities of neural networks. The underlying mechanism leverages biologically inspired feedback loops and memory mechanisms, mirroring aspects of human cognition. This research distinguishes itself from existing cognitive architectures that predominantly rely on single-modality models by introducing a more realistic simulation through the integration of multiple modalities. The architecture utilizes visual, auditory, and linguistic neural networks, demonstrating the potential for improved cognitive modeling and understanding of human information processing. This work provides a foundational approach for future research into complex cognitive functions. ---

title: Causal Discovery from Streaming Data with Bayesian Inference
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to causal discovery directly from streaming data utilizing Bayesian inference. Traditional causal discovery methods often require static datasets, posing a significant limitation when dealing with the continuous flow of information characteristic of real-world streaming environments. This work addresses this challenge by proposing a scalable Bayesian algorithm that dynamically updates a causal graph as new observations arrive. The algorithm incorporates temporal dependencies to refine the discovered relationships, mitigating the effects of noise and spurious correlations inherent in streaming data. The core of the method lies in continuously learning a probabilistic model of the data stream, allowing for the identification of causal links while accounting for the evolving nature of the system. This approach offers a practical solution for understanding dynamic systems in real-time, providing a mechanism for immediate insights and adaptive decision-making. The effectiveness of the method is demonstrated through a theoretical analysis and conceptual outline, highlighting its potential for applications in domains such as sensor networks, anomaly detection, and online learning systems.

title: Non-Linear Geometric Models: Adaptive Learning Strategies
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive learning strategy for non-linear geometric models, designed to enhance model generalization. Traditional learning algorithms often operate in a static manner, limiting the ability to effectively optimize model parameters for complex data distributions. This work proposes a dynamic adjustment mechanism based on data distribution, dynamically modifying learning parameters like learning rate and regularization coefficients. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of experiments on benchmark datasets, illustrating its ability to improve model performance compared to baseline methods. The core mechanism focuses on adapting the model's learning process to the inherent characteristics of the data, leading to more robust and accurate predictions.

title: Quantum Entanglement and Asymmetric Matrix Calculation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, holds the potential to revolutionize computation and simulation. This paper explores the development of a novel non-symmetric matrix calculation algorithm leveraging quantum entanglement to overcome limitations in current computational methods, particularly for complex quantum states. We introduce a new approach that circumvents the inherent asymmetries present in traditional matrix calculations, offering a promising path towards enhanced computational efficiency in both quantum computing and quantum simulation.

title: Attention Is All You Needed, Eventually: A Comparative Analysis Review of The Transformer Revolution in Sequence Modeling
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of The Transformer Revolution in Sequence Modeling in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of transformers and attention as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE-BASED ADAPTIVE LEARNING MEDIA TO SUPPORT INCLUSIVE EDUCATION FOR PUPILS WITH DIVERSE LEARNING NEEDS
authors: Moh. Aldrin Akbar Sitti Nur Alam
abstract: Inclusive education requires the availability of learning resources capable of accommodating the diversity of pupils’ abilities, characteristics, learning styles and individual needs. Conventional learning resources, which tend to be uniform, have not yet been fully able to provide a flexible and personalised learning experience, particularly for pupils with diverse learning needs. This article aims to analyse the concept, design and implementation of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based adaptive learning resources in support of inclusive education. This study employs a literature review using a descriptive-qualitative approach, analysing various scientific articles, academic books, reports from educational institutions, and relevant policy documents. The findings indicate that AI can help tailor content, difficulty levels, learning pace, presentation formats, activities, assessments, and feedback based on students’ profiles and progress. Adaptive learning media can also support accessibility through text-to-speech, speech-to-text, transcripts, visualisations, language simplification, and personalised learning recommendations. However, its implementation still faces challenges in the form of infrastructure limitations, teachers’ competence readiness, the digital divide, algorithmic bias, data security, and the need for human supervision. Therefore, the development of AI-based adaptive learning tools must be grounded in the principles of inclusive education, Universal Design for Learning, data protection, equity, transparency, and collaboration between teachers, pupils, parents, technology developers, and policymakers. When implemented responsibly, AI can serve as a strategic tool for creating learning experiences that are more personalised, flexible, accessible, and responsive to pupils’ diverse learning needs.

title: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence for Strategic Retail Promotions
abstract: The retail industry is undergoing a transformation due to the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in promotional strategies. Traditional methods like print ads, radio commercials, and in-store displays face challenges in today's dynamic retail environment, such as the inability to integrate with online platforms and provide interactive experiences. AI technologies like machine learning, natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning are redefining promotional strategies, enhancing customer engagement, and optimizing marketing efforts. AI-driven promotions are set to revolutionize the industry, with hyper-personalization and omnichannel retailing becoming key trends. However, challenges such as data privacy concerns, algorithmic biases, and the need to balance automation with human touch points are also addressed. The chapter provides strategic recommendations for retailers to harness AI effectively, including investing in cutting-edge tools and fostering collaborations with technology providers.

title: Data-Driven Conversational Marketing
abstract: Rapid advancements in artificial intelligence and digital communication technologies have transformed customer engagement in online marketplaces. Organizations increasingly use intelligent conversational systems to deliver personalized interactions, real-time assistance, and data-driven customer experiences across digital platforms. By analyzing browsing behavior, purchasing patterns, and consumer preferences, these systems help optimize customer journeys and improve engagement throughout the decision-making process. Intelligent chatbots enhance responsiveness, support interactive communication, and provide tailored recommendations that strengthen customer satisfaction and operational efficiency. However, concerns related to data privacy, transparency, algorithmic bias, and consumer trust continue to influence adoption and long-term effectiveness. Drawing on insights from digital marketing and consumer behavior research, this study examines how conversational technologies enhance customer engagement and support strategic marketing in evolving digital commerce ecosystems.

title: YesTrack: Referring Multi-Object Tracking via MLLM-based Yes/No Verification
abstract: Referring multi-object tracking (RMOT) aims to track every instance in a video that matches a given language expression. Despite the recent integration of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to enhance generalization, existing methods predominantly relegate them to the role of caption generators, necessitating external modules for final decision-making. This paradigm not only introduces extra latency but also severely underutilizes the inherent vision-language alignment capabilities of MLLMs. To address these limitations, we propose YesTrack, a novel two-stage RMOT method that reformulates referring as a discriminative task, directly leveraging MLLMs for Yes/No verification without explicit text generation. To further enhance the reliability and efficiency of this MLLM-based verification, we introduce two lightweight temporal consistency constraints: Temporal Confidence Prior (TCP) and Temporal Reference Propagation (TRP). We further validate the generality of this discriminative paradigm by proposing YesTrack-MOT, a straightforward yet highly effective instantiation for generic multi-object tracking (MOT). Experiments on Refer-KITTI and Refer-KITTI-V2 show that YesTrack significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods while maintaining high efficiency, even when implemented with the smallest variant of Qwen3-VL. Code is released at https://github.com/ggbondrighthere24/YesTrack.

title: Disease Burden over Skin Tone: Decomposing the Dermatology-AI Generalization Gap
abstract: Dermatology artificial intelligence (AI) models are predominantly trained on light-skinned, cancer-focused image collections, yet they are increasingly proposed for deployment in resource-constrained settings where patients differ from training populations along two confounded axes: skin tone and disease distribution. We investigate whether poor generalization is primarily caused by skin-tone underrepresentation or disease-distribution shift. We evaluate a cancer-trained baseline (ResNet-50 fine-tuned on HAM10000 and ISIC 2019), two dermatology foundation models (DermLIP and MONET), and a general-purpose vision model (DINOv3) as frozen feature extractors. Models are evaluated on a tone-stratified disease-matched dataset (Diverse Dermatology Images, DDI) and a disease-shifted tone-diverse dataset (Skin Condition Image Network, SCIN). Our results show that disease-distribution shift contributes more than skin tone in the evaluated settings. The cancer baseline decreases from 0.62 to 0.21 balanced accuracy when transferred to unfamiliar clinical conditions, while the within-disease skin-tone gap is smaller (0.10-0.18) and inconsistent. Label-free representation analysis shows that this failure reflects a representational limitation rather than only missing output labels: cancer-specialized features poorly cluster unfamiliar conditions (kNN purity lift +0.06 over chance), whereas dermatology-pretrained features retain stronger transferable structure (+0.23). Finally, we show that representation quality predicts recoverable performance under lightweight adaptation. Starting from dermatology foundation models, approximately ten labeled examples per clinical category recover most attainable performance. We release the evaluation protocol and code to support reproducible auditing of dermatology AI generalization.

title: 基于自旋的量子信息编码的计算范式
abstract: This paper presents a novel computational paradigm based on spin-based quantum information encoding. We explore the utilization of quantum spin properties to encode and transmit information, proposing a quantum computing algorithm designed to address complex problems. The core mechanism centers around leveraging the unique characteristics of spin, including its sensitivity to external fields, to establish robust and efficient data encoding. The paper details the design of a quantum algorithm that exploits these spin characteristics, offering a potential advancement over existing quantum computing approaches. We outline the key mathematical formulations and provide a preliminary assessment of the algorithm's potential performance. The research contributes to the exploration of spin-based quantum information encoding, with implications for the development of novel quantum algorithms and computational capabilities.

title: Teaching the Colossus to Say No: A State of the Art Review of Alignment Strategies for Large Language Models
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Alignment Strategies for Large Language Models in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of alignment and large language models as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Non-Linear Gradient Descent Algorithm with Adaptive Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel non-linear gradient descent algorithm designed to enhance model generalization capabilities through adaptive learning. Traditional gradient descent methods often rely on a fixed learning rate, which can be problematic in complex datasets. Our algorithm integrates gradient descent with an adaptive learning mechanism, dynamically adjusting the learning rate based on data-driven self-adaptation. This approach mitigates the risk of getting stuck in local optima and promotes more robust model performance. We detail the core mechanism, emphasizing the interplay between gradient descent and self-adaptation, and provide a comprehensive analysis of its performance compared to established techniques.

title: Adaptive Representation Learning for Sparse Data Streams
abstract: Sparse data streams present a significant challenge to traditional representation learning techniques. These streams are characterized by a severe lack of feature observations, leading to unstable and unreliable learned representations. This paper introduces a novel adaptive representation learning method designed specifically for sparse data streams. The core idea is to dynamically adjust the representation based on the observed frequencies of features. We leverage a hierarchical Bayesian model employing Gaussian processes to achieve this adaptation. The model's structure and parameters are continuously refined based on the observed feature distribution, enabling robust representation learning even with highly sparse data. The method's scalability and ability to handle infrequent feature occurrences are key advantages. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a theoretical analysis and illustrate its potential with a simplified example. The primary contribution lies in the adaptive structure of the learned representation, offering a more stable and informative representation compared to static methods.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Pattern Recognition
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to pattern recognition centered around the application of quantum entanglement to significantly enhance the accuracy and speed of identifying subtle patterns. Traditional pattern recognition methods often struggle with complex datasets and require extensive computational resources. We propose a system that utilizes a quantum-inspired 'state vector' to capture intricate patterns, offering a potential paradigm shift in this field. The core mechanism involves establishing entanglement between quantum systems, which allows for a unique level of correlation and information processing, ultimately leading to improved pattern identification capabilities. This work explores the theoretical foundations and preliminary experimental validation of this approach, aiming to demonstrate substantial improvements over existing techniques.

title: Dynamically Adaptive Neural Architecture Search via Evolutionary Algorithms and Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic neural architecture search (NAS) framework that addresses the limitations of existing methods, primarily their computational expense and lack of adaptability. Our approach combines the exploration capabilities of evolutionary algorithms with the learning efficiency of reinforcement learning to create a self-optimizing NAS process. The system utilizes an evolutionary algorithm to traverse the architecture search space, while a reinforcement learning agent learns to guide the evolutionary process, dynamically adjusting search parameters and strategies based on the observed performance of candidate architectures. This adaptive mechanism enables the system to tailor its search to the specific characteristics of the target problem, resulting in more efficient and effective architecture discovery. The key innovation lies in creating a feedback loop where the system continuously learns and refines its search strategy, leading to a significantly improved NAS performance compared to static NAS methods. The core claim of this work is that existing NAS methods often require extensive computation and are not adaptable to changing environments. The mechanism employs a hybrid approach where an evolutionary algorithm explores the architecture space, guided by a reinforcement learning agent that learns to optimize the search strategy based on the performance of candidate architectures.

title: Quantum Simulation of Brain Interfaces
abstract: This research explores the potential of quantum computing to revolutionize brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) by providing a fundamentally different approach to simulating neuronal activity and information transfer. The core claim posits that quantum algorithms can accurately model the intricate quantum effects within neural networks, leading to more precise brain interface design and therapeutic interventions. This study will detail the challenges and opportunities inherent in harnessing quantum mechanics for BCI applications, focusing on the unique capabilities of quantum bits (qubits) and their potential to overcome limitations of classical computing. We will examine current research directions, including the development of specialized quantum algorithms for neural network modeling, and discuss the technical and theoretical hurdles that must be addressed before practical implementation becomes feasible.

title: 基于自适应的神经元网络结构的全局信息传播
abstract: Distributed systems often face challenges with information propagation due to complex environments and data distribution. This paper introduces a novel approach to global information dissemination based on an adaptive neural network architecture. We propose a system where individual nodes within the network dynamically adjust their connection weights to facilitate information flow and enhance collaborative learning. The core of our design lies in a dynamically responsive neural network structure, enabling it to adapt to changing network conditions and optimize the dissemination of information across the system. This method significantly reduces information loss and improves the efficiency of collaborative learning compared to existing approaches. The paper details the architecture, training process, and performance evaluation, demonstrating the effectiveness of this adaptive system in a simulated environment.

title: Formal Modeling and Verification of Secure Multi-Party Computation using Homomorphic Encryption
abstract: Secure Multi-Party Computation (SMPC) enables multiple parties to compute a function without revealing their individual inputs. However, the complexity of these protocols makes rigorous verification challenging. This paper presents a formal model of SMPC leveraging homomorphic encryption and employs model checking to ascertain the security properties of the protocol. The SMPC protocol is represented as a cryptographic circuit, and security properties like privacy and integrity are formally defined using temporal logic. The core of the methodology lies in utilizing model checking algorithms to systematically verify that the circuit adheres to the specified security constraints. This approach provides a mathematically sound and verifiable framework for designing and analyzing SMPC protocols, addressing a critical gap in the current landscape of SMPC security assurance.

title: Information Geometry for Deep Learning Model Selection
abstract: Deep learning model selection remains a critical yet largely empirical process. Traditional methods frequently rely on heuristics and validation sets, offering limited theoretical justification. This paper proposes a novel approach leveraging information geometry to provide a rigorous framework for model selection. We argue that the loss landscape of a deep learning model can be interpreted as a Riemannian manifold, and that geometric properties such as Riemannian curvature and information divergence can be utilized to quantify the complexity and uncertainty associated with different models. Specifically, we introduce a method for characterizing the geometric structure of the loss landscape using these metrics, which can then be used to guide the selection of the optimal model. This approach offers a more principled and potentially more effective way to navigate the challenges of model selection in deep learning, moving beyond purely empirical strategies. The core idea is to treat model selection as a problem of finding the most stable and well-behaved point on the loss landscape, as determined by its geometric properties. We present a preliminary framework and discuss potential extensions and future research directions.

title: 基于自适应的机器学习的隐喻学习
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to machine learning called "基于自适应的机器学习的隐喻学习" (Adaptive Machine Learning Metaphor Learning). The core principle of this method is to leverage self-adaptive learning to construct and refine hidden models, dynamically adjusting their parameters based on data characteristics. Traditional machine learning often relies on fixed, pre-defined metaphors, which limits the model's adaptability to diverse tasks and datasets. This work proposes a system that automatically learns and optimizes these hidden models, resulting in improved model performance across various domains. We present a framework for self-adaptive learning of metaphors, incorporating a novel adaptation strategy that focuses on minimizing the discrepancy between the learned representation and the target domain. The research demonstrates the effectiveness of this method through comparisons with existing techniques and showcases its ability to generalize to unseen data.

title: Rare Events Bias
abstract: Rare events, where the outcome of interest occurs in fewer than 5% of observations, introduce systematic bias into standard logistic regression estimates. Coefficients tend to be biased away from zero and predicted probabilities underestimate event occurrence. This chapter examines the statistical mechanisms underlying rare events bias, including the first-order bias of maximum likelihood estimation and its dependence on events per variable. We present and compare four correction strategies: Firth&s;s penalized likelihood, bias-reduced generalised linear models, case-control sampling with intercept correction, and ROSE resampling. Through simulation studies and a fraud detection application, we demonstrate that bias-correction methods preserve coefficient interpretability while sampling-based approaches primarily improve classification. Practical guidance on method selection, appropriate evaluation metrics, and transparent reporting is provided.

title: Seeing Less Is Not Seeing Safely: Privacy Leakage from Task-Scoped Robot Perception Exports
abstract: Domestic robots rely on rich perception to operate in private homes, but privacy risk persists even when raw sensor data remain local. Structured representations exported to downstream planners, cloud services, logs, or learning pipelines can still reveal household information through semantics, geometry, spatial structure, and task targets. We introduce Task-Functional Perception Distillation (TFPD), a task-scoped representation-export framework that keeps rich perception local and profiles downstream exports according to task utility, direct exposure, and multiple residual inference risks. Using 120 AI2-THOR scenes with scene-disjoint train/validation/test splits, frozen attacker selection, and representation-aware held-out attacks, we evaluate navigation, collision checking, and object-goal execution. Three navigation exports achieve identical success (1.000) and mean path ratio (0.898), yet representation-level linkability ranges from 0.532 to 0.970. Replacing an explicit target label with a target region reduces target-category macro-F1 from 1.000 to 0.077 while preserving success at 0.995, while geometric coarsening reduces object-category macro-F1 from 0.704 to 0.556 at a measurable collision-utility cost. A ProcTHOR replication preserves the navigation task-equivalence/privacy-inequivalence finding while changing the relative ordering of normalized and topological exports. These results show that neither field removal nor stronger abstraction induces a universal privacy ordering and motivate task-specific, multi-risk evaluation of the complete public representation.

title: Discriminative World Models for Web Agents
abstract: Recent web agents use world models for test-time action selection by sampling candidate actions, predicting the resulting web states, and ranking them with a ranker model or a Process Reward Model (PRM). These world models are typically trained via supervised next-state prediction to generate fixed representations like HTML or AXTree snapshots. However, this objective is misaligned with the downstream ranker, which relies on predicted states being discriminative across candidates to accurately score them. title: A Computational Comparison of Fourier Spectral Differentiation and Spatial Automatic Differentiation in Periodic Physics-Informed Neural Networks
abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) commonly evaluate the spatial derivatives appearing in partial differential equation residuals using automatic differentiation (AD), whose computational and memory costs can become substantial when multiple or high-order derivatives are required. We perform a controlled comparison of spatial AD and Fourier spectral differentiation in periodic physical-space PINNs. Within each paired experiment, the neural representation, temporal differentiation, optimizer, sampling procedure, and training schedule are held fixed, so that the two cases differ only in the spatial differentiation procedure. For the Fourier variant, network outputs are evaluated on a uniform periodic grid and transformed to Fourier space, where spatial derivatives are obtained through spectral multiplication and the same Fourier coefficients are reused across derivative orders. We compare the two procedures in standard PINNs for the Allen--Cahn and Korteweg--de Vries equations and in Causal PINNs for the Allen--Cahn, Korteweg--de Vries, and Kuramoto--Sivashinsky equations. Across these five equation--framework settings, Fourier differentiation yields mean paired end-to-end training speedups ranging from $2.90\times$ to $18.52\times$ and reduces peak allocated graphics processing unit (GPU) memory by $68.7\%$--$94.1\%$. The final relative $L_2$ errors remain of the same order, with neither differentiation procedure showing a consistent accuracy advantage. For the one-dimensional periodic benchmarks considered here, Fourier spectral differentiation therefore provides substantially lower training time and memory usage than spatial AD while retaining comparable solution error, at the cost of requiring a uniform structured spatial grid.

title: An Entanglement-Assisted Stabilizer Framework for Distributed Sensing of Local Phases
abstract: Distributed quantum sensing requires spatially separated probes to acquire local parameters while maintaining compatibility with network-level quantum information processing. We develop an entanglement-assisted stabilizer framework based on the extended structure of entanglement-assisted quantum error-correcting (EAQEC) codes, in which the remote halves of pre-shared ebits are used directly as local phase probes while the joint state simultaneously carries an encoded logical subsystem. Each remote probe acquires a local Z-axis phase and subsequently returns through an X-type noise channel. Within the extended EAQEC stabilizer structure, the stabilizer containing $X_{B_j}$ provides phase-dependent measurement statistics, whereas its partner containing $Z_{B_j}$ records the corresponding return-error syndrome. A graph-code formulation is introduced to make this structure explicit, together with an illustrative [[5,1,3;2]] construction. We further show that, conditioned on the joint sensing-and-syndrome measurement record, the post-sensing state differs from the original encoded state only by a known Pauli transformation, so that the logical information remains available for subsequent encoded operations. For the local-phase model considered here, the stabilizer readout attains the available quantum Fisher information, while the finite-shot estimator approaches the corresponding $1/\sqrt{M}$ scaling as the number of repetitions increases. The framework therefore provides a common entanglement-assisted stabilizer structure for distributed local-phase sensing, restricted return-error identification, and post-sensing logical-state retention, without relying on an intrinsic metrological enhancement from EAQEC itself.

title: Remote engineering of particle-like topologies to visualise entanglement dynamics
abstract: Skyrmions are a particle-like topology with a quantized skyrmion number, realized across condensed matter and photonic platforms alike. In quantum photonics, they constitute an emerging resource, promising robust quantum information encoding, so far realized as single-photon and bi-photon entangled states. Here we report the first visualization of tripartite entanglement dynamics through topological structure using spin-skyrmion entangled states, where the topology of a single photon is remotely controlled through the spin of its entangled partner. We visualize our tripartite state theoretically by introducing the notion of a topological Bloch sphere that completely captures the entanglement and topological features of the state. By leveraging this state, we realize the first quantum multiskyrmions, comprising multiple localized skyrmions within a single structure, that emulate signatures of their magnetic counterparts. We verify this experimentally and show that traversing our topological sphere reveals entanglement-driven particle-like motion of the localized topological structures. These dynamics unveil a physical manifestation of tripartite entanglement correlations which we illustrate by example of GHZ-like states, enabling a visualization of multiple Bell states encoded within our system. Our work opens exciting possibilities for quantum sensing by mapping complex quantum channel features onto topological observables of multipartite states and offers a promising avenue for harnessing quantum topologies for multi-level encoding quantum communication schemes.

title: Looking Things Up Before Speaking: A State of the Art Review of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of RAG and retrieval as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: 基于量子自组织的分布式学习框架
abstract: This paper introduces a novel distributed learning framework based on the principles of quantum self-organization. The framework leverages the unique properties of quantum self-organization to achieve distributed learning and model prediction, offering a fundamentally different approach compared to traditional distributed learning methods. We detail the framework's architecture, explain the core mechanisms driving its functionality, and highlight its advantages, including inherent fault tolerance, adaptability, and potential for efficient resource utilization. The paper demonstrates the framework's effectiveness through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental results, showcasing its capability to outperform existing methods in specific scenarios. Ultimately, this research establishes a foundation for a new paradigm in distributed learning, driven by the transformative potential of quantum self-organization.

title: Quantum Hiding Matrix Optimization
abstract: Quantum Hiding Matrix Optimization (QHMO) presents a novel quantum computation paradigm that leverages dynamic parameter adjustments through a hidden matrix optimization algorithm. Traditional quantum algorithms are constrained by fixed parameters, limiting their potential for optimization and efficiency. This research introduces QHMO, a quantum algorithm capable of adapting to changing system conditions, thereby achieving improved performance. The core mechanism centers around creating a quantum "hiding matrix" that dynamically modifies the quantum state, allowing for optimized computation. We detail the algorithm's design, the underlying mathematical principles, and its potential impact on quantum computation. This paper explores the advantages of dynamic parameter adjustment and its implications for enhancing quantum algorithms.

title: Formal Verification of Adaptive Compiler Optimization
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to compiler optimization by integrating formal verification techniques. The core idea is to leverage mathematical models of program behavior, coupled with formal verification tools, to guarantee the correctness and safety of compiler optimization algorithms. Traditional compiler optimization often relies on heuristics and empirical analysis, leading to potential errors and security vulnerabilities. Our proposed system dynamically adapts optimization strategies based on the verification results, ensuring that only safe and correct transformations are applied. This adaptive approach significantly enhances the reliability of the compilation process and allows for the construction of more robust and secure software. The system employs a feedback loop where verification results guide the optimization engine, minimizing the risk of introducing unintended behavior. The primary contribution is a framework for self-verifying compiler optimization, offering a pathway towards greater confidence in compiled code.

title: Quantum State Superposition-Based Database Query
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to database querying by leveraging the principles of quantum state superposition. Traditional database queries are inherently sequential, often leading to performance bottlenecks, particularly with large datasets. This research proposes a paradigm shift where database queries are translated into quantum bits (qubits) existing in superposition states. Utilizing the inherent parallelism of quantum computers, we aim to execute multiple queries concurrently, dramatically accelerating the overall query process. The core claim is that superposition allows for parallel execution of database queries, significantly boosting efficiency. This work outlines the theoretical framework, identifies key challenges, and proposes a methodology for implementing superposition-based database querying. The focus remains on the conceptual design and potential benefits, without engaging in experimental validation.

title: Decentralized Differential Privacy using Secure Multi-Party Computation
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for achieving differential privacy in decentralized systems. The core idea leverages the combination of Secure Multi-Party Computation (SMPC) and distributed aggregation protocols. SMPC allows multiple parties to collaboratively compute statistics while preserving the privacy of individual data contributions. Subsequent application of differential privacy mechanisms to the aggregated results guarantees differential privacy. This approach offers a practical solution for privacy-preserving data analysis in scenarios where centralized computation is infeasible or undesirable. The framework is designed to be modular, enabling flexibility in choosing specific SMPC protocols and differential privacy algorithms. We demonstrate the feasibility and potential of this approach through theoretical analysis and outline key design considerations for implementation.

title: Quantum Entanglement Encoding for Distributed Computing Architecture
abstract: This paper proposes a novel distributed computing architecture leveraging multi-body quantum entanglement for enhanced computational capabilities. The core claim centers on utilizing entangled states to facilitate scalable distributed quantum computing, potentially enabling superluminal information transfer and highly efficient parallel processing. The proposed mechanism involves designing a protocol based on entangled state superposition and measurement for node-to-node quantum information transmission, coupled with quantum decoherence mitigation and error correction techniques to ensure computational reliability. The architecture addresses the inherent communication bottlenecks in traditional distributed computing, offering a pathway to genuine parallel computation through quantum entanglement. This represents a crucial advancement in the field of quantum computing. title: Quantum Machine Learning: Style Transfer and Knowledge Fusion
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) represents a paradigm shift in computational science, offering the potential for unprecedented speed and efficiency in complex calculations. This paper investigates the integration of style transfer and knowledge fusion into quantum machine learning (QML) models. The core claim is that leveraging quantum computer properties, particularly superposition and entanglement, can effectively enhance the generalization capabilities of QML models by introducing stylistic elements from classical machine learning. We explore the application of quantum techniques to model the transfer of stylistic patterns and the incorporation of knowledge from existing datasets, aiming to improve model robustness and adaptability. The paper details the mechanisms employed, highlighting the role of quantum properties in facilitating these processes.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel Quantum State Reconstruction Algorithm (QSRA) designed to precisely reconstruct complex quantum states from uncertain initial conditions. The algorithm leverages the principles of quantum entanglement and measurement to achieve a significant improvement in quantum computation efficiency. We demonstrate the algorithm's ability to reconstruct intricate quantum states with enhanced accuracy, offering a practical pathway toward optimizing quantum computations. This research addresses a critical challenge in quantum information processing, focusing on achieving precise state reconstruction and utilizing quantum computation to optimize the process.

title: Dynamic Topological Logic
abstract: This paper introduces Dynamic Topological Logic (DTL), a novel approach to knowledge graph reasoning that leverages distributed computing and blockchain technology. The core claim is to develop a logic system where node states dynamically adjust their logical relationships, forming adaptive knowledge graph inference systems. This is achieved through a distributed node network built upon a blockchain, where node states (representing truth values, probabilities, etc.) are updated using probability transition functions. Logical relationships are dynamically adjusted based on the correlations between these node states, enabling real-time inference for uncertain information and dynamic environments. The key innovation lies in the system's ability to model the dynamic evolution of node states within knowledge graphs – a capability currently lacking in existing logical systems, coupled with a scalable distributed inference mechanism. The proposed framework offers a path toward more robust and adaptable reasoning systems for complex, evolving data landscapes. ---

title: Quantum-Inspired Algorithm for Optimal Data Compression
abstract: This paper proposes a novel data compression algorithm inspired by quantum mechanics, specifically leveraging superposition and interference principles. Traditional data compression techniques, such as Huffman coding and Lempel-Ziv, rely on statistical redundancy and dictionary-based methods, which are fundamentally limited by the inherent complexity and non-stationarity of real-world data. Our algorithm aims to transcend these limitations by directly exploiting correlations within the data through a simulated quantum-inspired approach. The core idea involves representing data elements in a superposition of states, allowing for interference to amplify correlations and reduce redundancy. We introduce a mathematical framework to describe this process, utilizing concepts from linear algebra and probability theory. This framework enables the development of a compression model that dynamically adapts to the data's statistical properties. The proposed algorithm is evaluated theoretically, demonstrating its potential to achieve significantly higher compression ratios compared to conventional methods. Key performance indicators, such as compression ratio, bit rate, and computational complexity, are analyzed. The algorithm's ability to handle non-stationary data distributions is a central focus. The theoretical analysis provides a foundation for future experimental validation and optimization.

title: Neural Symbolic Systems: Integrating Neural Networks with Symbolic Reasoning Engines
abstract: This paper presents a novel neural symbolic system designed to address the limitations of purely neural or purely symbolic approaches to artificial intelligence. The core idea is to seamlessly integrate the pattern recognition prowess of neural networks with the logical inference capabilities of symbolic reasoning engines. We propose a framework where a neural network acts as a feature extractor, translating raw sensory data into symbolic representations. Subsequently, a symbolic reasoning engine leverages these representations to perform logical deductions and ultimately arrive at conclusions. This hybrid system aims to leverage the strengths of both paradigms, offering a potentially more robust and interpretable pathway to intelligent behavior. The system is described in detail, outlining the architecture, the interaction between the neural and symbolic components, and the underlying principles. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a theoretical framework, focusing on the challenges and opportunities associated with the integration of these two distinct computational models. The system's design emphasizes modularity and adaptability, allowing for the incorporation of diverse neural network architectures and symbolic reasoning systems. Future research directions are discussed, including exploring different neural network architectures for symbolic representation learning and investigating methods for optimizing the interaction between the two components.

title: Self-Adaptive Quantum State Topology Optimization
abstract: Quantum state topology optimization is a challenging task requiring precise control over quantum states. This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive quantum state topology optimization algorithm, leveraging the inherent properties of quantum states to guide the optimization process. We propose a framework that dynamically adjusts the quantum state parameters based on feedback from the optimization process, enabling a more efficient and robust optimization. The core mechanism centers around a quantum state evolution driven by a feedback loop, resulting in improved performance compared to existing classical optimization techniques. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations and provide a detailed analysis of its performance characteristics. The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency make it a promising approach for tackling complex quantum optimization problems.

title: AI-Powered Conversational Marketing in Hospitality
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered conversational marketing is rapidly transforming the hospitality industry by enabling real-time, personalized, and interactive engagement with guests. Intelligent chatbots, driven by natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning algorithms, are redefining how hotels, resorts, and travel platforms communicate with customers across multiple touchpoints. This study explores the role of AI-driven chatbots in enhancing guest experiences, from pre-booking inquiries and reservation assistance to in-stay services and post-visit feedback collection. By offering 24/7 availability, multilingual support, and data-driven personalization, conversational marketing tools significantly improve customer satisfaction, operational efficiency, and brand loyalty. The chapter further examines the integration of chatbots within omnichannel communication strategies, enabling seamless interactions across websites, mobile applications, and social media platforms.

title: Optimized Matrix-Product State Simulations of Quantum Error Correction Circuits
abstract: Simulating quantum error correction (QEC) circuits including non-Clifford gates at scale is important to accelerate progress toward fault-tolerant quantum computing. Here we demonstrate that matrix product state (MPS) techniques can handle many QEC circuits exactly and without restriction on gate types. Crucially, we find that MPS efficiency depends sensitively on implementation choices, and we introduce a series of targeted optimizations that reduce bond dimensions and simulation time by several orders of magnitude compared to naive approaches. We illustrate this with examples including: (a) a rotated surface code quantum memory up to distance 11, (b) logical Bell-state preparation up to distance 9, (c) a 15-to-1 magic-state distillation circuit including hundreds of QEC rounds that we optimize to be simulated with only 11 logical qubits (187 physical qubits) and a maximal bond dimension of 64 in under 40 seconds, and (d) a narrow, deep random circuit that scales linearly with the number of T gates. These results demonstrate the importance of circuit-level optimizations and position MPS as a valuable complement to near-Clifford simulators for QEC circuits.

title: Learning-Based Reconstruction Attacks on Coordinate-Obfuscated Point Clouds
abstract: Volumetric video based on point cloud representations enables immersive virtual and augmented reality applications but introduces significant challenges for efficient and secure content delivery. Prior work proposed a selective coordinate encryption framework for point clouds that encrypts only a subset of coordinates, reducing computational costs while visually degrading unauthorized content. However, it remains unclear whether the remaining unencrypted information is sufficient to enable content reconstruction. In this paper, we evaluate the robustness of selective coordinate encryption against machine learning-based reconstruction attacks. We consider an attacker with access to selectively encrypted point clouds attempting to recover encrypted coordinates without decryption by exploiting spatial and geometric correlations in the unencrypted data. We evaluate PointNet and Random Forest models under two encryption granularities: \texttt{X}, where all $X$ coordinates are encrypted, and \texttt{2X}, where every second $X$ coordinate is encrypted. Our results show that reconstructing fully encrypted $X$ coordinates remains challenging, whereas the \texttt{2X} scheme leaks sufficient information through neighboring coordinates to enable accurate reconstruction. These findings demonstrate that the security of selective coordinate encryption depends strongly on encryption granularity.

title: MeanField Surrogate Modeling for Scalable Runtime Scheduling of Concurrent Heterogeneous AI Inference on Shared GPUs
abstract: Deploying heterogeneous AI models concurrently on a shared GPU introduces resource contention that complicates runtime scheduling. While surrogate models avoid costly online benchmarking, their profiling requirements typically grow combinatorially with the number of co-running models, limiting scalability. We propose a MeanField surrogate that predicts per-model performance from local configuration and aggregate GPU state rather than explicitly modeling all joint interactions. Experiments on concurrent LLM and vision workloads across $N \in \{2,3,4,5,6\}$ show high predictive accuracy ($R^2 \approx 0.96$) with an empirical sample budget that grows approximately linearly in $N$, in contrast to the combinatorial cost of fully joint profiling. Integrated into a genetic algorithm scheduler, the surrogate scales to an $N=5$ problem with 78,732 feasible joint configurations, remaining within 0.10% of the exhaustive search with zero SLA violations across eight dynamic workload scenarios, while complete online GA decisions take 26 ms median, about $5\times$ faster than exhaustive surrogate search.

title: 基于量子自旋的动态几何变形控制
abstract: Quantum systems often exhibit complex and tunable geometric structures, which can dramatically influence their performance. This paper presents a novel dynamic geometric deformation control algorithm based on the intrinsic properties of quantum spin. We leverage the self-associativity of quantum spin to iteratively optimize the geometry of a quantum system, allowing for dynamic adjustment and optimization. This approach offers a unique pathway towards enhancing quantum device performance through enhanced control over system structure. The algorithm's core mechanism centers on exploiting self-relatedness to generate complex geometric patterns and subsequently optimizing the system through iterative control of these patterns. This offers a potential advantage over traditional geometric optimization techniques, particularly in scenarios requiring complex and dynamic adjustments. The work addresses the limitations of existing approaches by providing a framework for adaptive geometric shaping of quantum systems.

title: Quantum Entanglement and Adaptive Quantum Computing: A Novel Approach
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre phenomenon where two or more particles become linked and share the same fate, holds immense promise for revolutionary advancements in computation. This paper explores the potential of adaptive quantum computing, a paradigm shift from static quantum algorithms, leveraging the dynamic properties of entangled qubits. We propose a new computational framework predicated on the self-adjusting nature of entangled states, aiming to enhance performance in complex problems. The core mechanism centers around designing a quantum algorithm that autonomously manipulates the entanglement to achieve optimal results. This work presents a novel approach to quantum computation, driven by the inherent potential of entangled states to adapt to problem-solving challenges. The proposed methodology offers a distinct path toward overcoming limitations of current quantum computing architectures.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding and Verification
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a perplexing phenomenon where two or more particles become linked in such a way that they share the same fate no matter how far apart they are, holds immense potential for revolutionizing information security. This paper explores the utilization of quantum entanglement to design a novel information encoding system, termed "Quantum Entanglement Key Distribution" (QEKD). We propose a mechanism that leverages entanglement to achieve unprecedented levels of security and efficient data transfer, fundamentally challenging traditional cryptographic approaches. The core of this work centers on the creation of a QEKD system that transcends classical encryption methods through the inherent properties of quantum entanglement. This system offers the potential for information security significantly surpassing current methods, promising enhanced privacy and accelerated data transfer.

title: 基于自组织网络的机器学习 (Self-Organizing Network Machine Learning)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning model based on a self-organizing network architecture. Traditional machine learning models often rely on fixed structures, and this research proposes a model that leverages the inherent structural properties of self-organizing networks to enhance learning efficiency and generalization capabilities. The core of our approach involves designing and implementing a self-organizing network that adapts its parameters based on the input data, promoting robust and efficient learning. We detail the model's architecture, training process, and evaluation results, demonstrating its potential for improved performance compared to conventional methods. The focus is on creating a model that intrinsically learns patterns and relationships within the data, allowing for more nuanced and adaptable solutions.

title: Probability Space Dynamical Systems Adaptive Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel adaptive optimization algorithm for complex systems, leveraging the inherent probabilistic nature of dynamical systems. Traditional optimization methods often rely on manually designed parameters, limiting their ability to adapt to evolving environments. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts the probability distribution of the dynamical system, enabling the algorithm to converge to optimal solutions even in the presence of uncertainty. This approach is validated through extensive simulations and demonstrates improved performance compared to existing methods, particularly in scenarios involving complex, non-linear dynamics.

title: Too Simple, Too Complex, Just Right: A State of the Art Review of Inductive Biases in Deep Learning Architectures
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Inductive Biases in Deep Learning Architectures in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of deep learning and inductive bias as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Differential Privacy with Adaptive Noise Calibration
abstract: This paper introduces a novel differential privacy mechanism employing adaptive noise calibration. Traditional approaches to differential privacy often rely on fixed noise scales, which can be overly conservative, leading to significant utility loss. Our method addresses this limitation by leveraging a machine learning model to predict the sensitivity of a given query and dynamically adjust the noise level. This approach minimizes privacy loss while maintaining acceptable utility levels. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our mechanism through theoretical analysis and a conceptual framework, outlining a practical implementation strategy. The core innovation lies in the intelligent, data-driven calibration of noise, representing a significant step forward in achieving both privacy and utility in data analysis.

title: Distributed Federated Learning with Differential Privacy for Personalized Models
abstract: Federated learning (FL) presents a promising approach to training machine learning models across decentralized devices while preserving data privacy. However, traditional FL methods often lack sufficient privacy guarantees, leaving users vulnerable to privacy breaches. This work proposes a novel framework for distributed federated learning incorporating differential privacy (DP). Our approach enhances the standard FL process by adding noise to the model updates, effectively masking individual user contributions. This guarantees a rigorous privacy budget, quantified by the ε and δ parameters of the DP mechanism. The resulting system enables personalized model training – adapting the global model to individual user data – while maintaining strong privacy protections. We outline the core components of the system, including client selection, local model training with DP noise injection, and aggregation of noisy updates. The theoretical analysis demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving strong privacy guarantees alongside reasonable model accuracy. The presented framework provides a viable path for building trust-worthy and privacy-preserving collaborative learning systems.
