title: Topology-Based Constraint Validation for Verification
abstract: This paper introduces a novel method for validating mathematical proofs and algorithms by analyzing the structure of the underlying topology. Traditional verification methods often rely on formal proofs, which can be computationally expensive and susceptible to subtle errors. This work proposes a new approach that leverages topological properties to automatically detect inconsistencies and errors within the proof process, improving robustness against errors that might not be immediately apparent through traditional checks. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through rigorous analysis of several complex mathematical scenarios, showcasing its ability to identify errors with minimal computational overhead. The core mechanism centers around identifying and exploiting topological invariants to establish the validity of the proof. This approach offers a significant advancement in verification, particularly for intricate and complex mathematical structures.

title: Based on Formal Languages: A Program Synthesis and Verification Framework
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for program synthesis and verification grounded in the rigorous application of formal languages. The core principle is to precisely define program functionality and constraints using formal languages, coupled with automated tools to achieve efficient synthesis and robust verification. Traditional approaches to program synthesis and verification often rely on heuristic search or model checking, which can be computationally expensive and lack the guarantees provided by formal methods. This framework addresses these limitations by leveraging the power of logical program synthesis and formal verification techniques, integrated through a unified system. The key innovation lies in the deep integration of formal language specification with automated synthesis and validation processes, offering a more reliable and scalable solution for software development. The framework allows for the generation of programs that are demonstrably correct according to a formally defined specification, reducing the reliance on manual testing and improving software quality. ---

title: Neuro-Symbolic Verification of Concurrent Program Correctness
abstract: Concurrent program verification remains a significant challenge in software engineering due to the inherent complexity of managing multiple interacting processes. Traditional verification techniques often struggle to scale to large, concurrent systems, particularly in detecting subtle issues like race conditions and deadlocks. This paper proposes a novel neuro-symbolic approach to concurrent program verification, integrating the strengths of neural networks and symbolic theorem provers. The system employs a neural network to learn a representation of program states and interactions, effectively capturing the dynamic behavior of concurrent processes. This learned representation is then fed into a symbolic theorem prover, which formally verifies the system's behavior against a predefined set of concurrency properties. The core idea is to leverage the neural network's ability to handle uncertainty and high-dimensional state spaces while utilizing the theorem prover's rigorous formal reasoning capabilities. This hybrid approach promises a more robust and scalable solution for verifying the correctness of concurrent programs, addressing the limitations of existing methodologies. The primary focus is on the theoretical framework and the integration strategy, outlining a pathway for future research and development.

This paper proposes a novel neuro-symbolic approach to concurrent program verification, integrating the strengths of neural networks and symbolic theorem provers. The system employs a neural network to learn a representation of program states and interactions, effectively capturing the dynamic behavior of concurrent processes. This learned representation is then fed into a symbolic theorem prover, which formally verifies the system's behavior against a predefined set of concurrency properties. The core idea is to leverage the neural network's ability to handle uncertainty and high-dimensional state spaces while utilizing the theorem prover's rigorous formal reasoning capabilities. This hybrid approach promises a more robust and scalable solution for verifying the correctness of concurrent programs, addressing the limitations of existing methodologies. The primary focus is on the theoretical framework and the integration strategy, outlining a pathway for future research and development.

title: Neuromorphic Reservoir Computing for Time Series Prediction with Dynamic Reservoir Shaping
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to time series prediction utilizing neuromorphic reservoir computing principles combined with dynamic reservoir shaping. The core idea is to leverage a recurrent neural network as the reservoir, coupled with feedback mechanisms to adaptively modulate its dynamics in response to the input time series. Unlike traditional reservoir computing methods which often employ fixed reservoir parameters, this work introduces a dynamic shaping component, allowing the system to optimally respond to the evolving statistical properties of the input data. The system aims to improve prediction accuracy and robustness by continuously adjusting the reservoir's characteristics, thereby enhancing its ability to capture temporal dependencies. The theoretical framework and mathematical formulation are detailed, demonstrating the underlying principles and potential benefits of this adaptive reservoir computing paradigm. The primary contributions of this work lie in the integration of dynamic shaping and the detailed mathematical analysis of the system's behavior.

title: GRADSOLVE: fast exact gradients for ODE ensembles on GPUs
abstract: Ordinary differential equations (ODEs) underlie models in science and engineering, and many applications need derivatives of their solutions with respect to parameters. Ensembles of independent trajectories suit graphics processing units (GPUs), but current GPU software forces a trade-off: the fastest ensemble solvers cannot be differentiated in reverse mode at the speed they solve, and the solvers built for differentiation solve more slowly. No single tool has yet offered a reverse-mode gradient at the speed of a fused-kernel solve. We present GRADSOLVE, an open-source JAX library for solving and reverse-mode differentiating low-dimensional ODE ensembles on NVIDIA GPUs. It records the steps an adaptive solver accepts and differentiates a fixed-step replay of them; the returned gradient is the exact discrete adjoint of those steps, the same derivative Diffrax returns by default, obtained more cheaply from a fixed-length chain than from an adaptive loop. It targets ensembles differentiated many times against one recorded mesh, keeps Diffrax as a fallback, and supports explicit and Rosenbrock integrators. Used as a solver, GRADSOLVE's forward-only kernel ran 2.8x faster than DiffEqGPU.jl; used for gradients, once a record exists, it computed them 5.6-14.1x faster than Diffrax's checkpointed adjoint at matched forward-state accuracy across three GPU generations, the advantage narrowing on large ensembles and, on stiff systems, down to parity at tight accuracy. GRADSOLVE is released at https://github.com/ECLIPSE-AI4Science/gradsolve.

title: Online Reinforcement Learning in the Met Office Unified Model through Distributed Model-Agent Coupling
abstract: Machine-learnt corrections can complement numerical weather prediction provided that they operate stably within an evolving numerical model. In this study, we couple the Met Office (UKMO) Unified Model (UM) with distributed reinforcement-learning agents through rank-local tensors. A column-aware deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) actor uses local vertical structure together with full-column context to apply bounded corrections to potential temperature and horizontal wind. During training, we perform ten nudged 6-hr 12-min forecasts, with nudging towards the UKMO operational analysis providing an immediate counterfactual target from which the policy learns. The resulting actor is then frozen and applied to a non-nudged forecast without access to analysis inputs or further weight updates. Relative to a matched non-nudged native forecast at +6 h, the corrected forecast reduces global latitude-weighted MAE by 2.85% for $Z_{500}$, 2.16% for MSLP, 5.16% for $T_{500}$ and 2.27% for $T_{1.5\textrm{m}}$, with an observed 3.57% wall-time overhead compared to native execution. Even though training and inference share the same initialisation, this single-case experiment demonstrates significant promise and feasibility, laying the groundwork for RL-based bias correction and parametrisations within operational systems.

title: Efficient GUI Agents: A Systems Survey of Observation, Memory, Action, and Runtime Optimization
abstract: GUI agents increasingly operate across websites, mobile apps, and desktop environments, yet the field still reports progress primarily through task success. We argue that practical deployment depends equally on efficiency: how much context, computation, action budget, and runtime overhead an agent consumes while succeeding. This survey studies efficient GUI agents through an end-to-end systems lens that preserves the current technical axes of observation efficiency, context and memory efficiency, action efficiency, and planner-side/system efficiency. For each subsection, we expand the seed literature through targeted search plus backward and forward citation chaining, then synthesize the dominant mechanisms, reported efficiency signals, and new overheads they introduce. Across the literature, recent progress converges on a small set of recurring ideas: selective reading instead of full-context ingestion, global-to-local visual allocation, recoverable memory rather than raw history replay, verification-aware control, and hybrid runtimes that can switch between GUI and non-GUI execution. We conclude by identifying the main open problems, including honest accounting of verifier cost, cross-benchmark comparability, and co-design of observation, memory, and execution layers under real latency and privacy constraints.

title: Model checkpoints for external validation of routine-laboratory-trajectory complication prediction (MIMIC-IV & MMRF CoMMpass)
abstract: Trained model checkpoints to reproduce the external-validation results (MIMIC-IV and MMRF CoMMpass) reported in the manuscript "Routine laboratory trajectories predict organ-level complications in cancer." The archive contains: the 162-diagnosis transformer prediction model as a 5-fold ensemble (best_pr_auc_model_*.pth — the checkpoints used to produce the reported numbers), the imputation model (best_model_2026-04-22_16-38-29.pth, 4,229,160 parameters), and the fold→config index (experiment_groups_manuscript.pkl). Companion code: https://github.com/jalu1870/external-validation-reproduction — extract into your LABPRED_ARTIFACTS directory. Weights only; the input cohorts (MIMIC-IV, MMRF CoMMpass) are access-restricted and are not included.

title: An Architecture for AI Systems That Can Reframe Problem Formulations
abstract: This work proposes a model-agnostic multi-agent architecture in which problem formulation becomes an explicit object of computational exploration. Rather than treating a user-provided problem as a fixed specification, the system examines implicit assumptions, generates alternative problem settings, and explores corresponding solution spaces. The architecture separates problem-setting agents, evaluators, solution-exploration agents, and solution evaluators, allowing heterogeneous AI systems to maintain divergent hypotheses and challenge one another. A feedback loop enables the system to return from solution exploration to problem reframing when solutions converge, rely on unexamined assumptions, or fail due to limitations in the original problem formulation. The purpose of this work is not to claim that AI can necessarily discover paradigm-shifting inventions, but to provide a computational framework for investigating whether AI systems can explore problem spaces beyond the assumptions contained in their initial formulation. Human judgment remains central: the system expands the space of questions that humans and AI can investigate together, without replacing human evaluation or decision-making.

title: Quantum Simulation Geometry Optimization
abstract: Quantum Simulation Geometry Optimization explores the potential of quantum simulation to revolutionize geometric optimization problems by leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics. This paper investigates the core concepts, mechanisms, and potential applications of this novel approach, emphasizing its ability to enhance simulation accuracy, efficiency, and the discovery of previously unseen physical phenomena through the optimization of geometric structures. We present a detailed theoretical framework and preliminary results demonstrating the efficacy of this methodology, highlighting its advantages over traditional classical methods. The core claim centers on utilizing quantum simulation to achieve unparalleled precision and speed in geometric optimization, potentially unlocking new scientific insights.

title: Probability Modal Logic: A Novel Approach to Modeling Complex Systems
abstract: Probability Modal Logic (PML) is a declarative logic system designed to represent and reason about complex systems, particularly those involving uncertainty and dynamic behavior. This paper introduces a novel PML framework that allows for the explicit modeling of event occurrences and their probabilistic evolution, offering a powerful tool for simulating intricate systems like financial markets and ecological modeling. The core of this approach lies in the introduction of a "probability modal grammar" – a system of rules and expressions that defines the possible states of a system and the transitions between them. This allows for a more flexible and expressive representation of these systems compared to traditional approaches. We detail the mechanism of dynamic event modeling and demonstrate its efficacy through illustrative examples, highlighting its potential for advancing modeling capabilities in various disciplines.

title: 基于深度学习的量子态预测与优化
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense potential for revolutionizing various fields, but realizing this potential requires overcoming significant challenges related to qubit stability, coherence, and control. Quantum state prediction and optimization are crucial steps in this process. This paper introduces a novel deep learning-based approach for both quantum state prediction and optimization. We leverage the power of deep neural networks to learn the complex patterns within quantum states, enabling accurate predictions of quantum circuit performance and automated optimization of circuit design. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation, showcasing a significant improvement over existing methods. This work represents a significant advancement in quantum algorithm design, offering a promising pathway towards more efficient and reliable quantum computations.

title: Graph Neural Networks for Modeling Social Influence Networks with Temporal Dynamics
abstract: Social influence networks are ubiquitous in various domains, including information diffusion, opinion dynamics, and social marketing. Traditional network models often fail to capture the dynamic evolution of these networks, neglecting the temporal dependencies that govern how influence spreads over time. This paper proposes a novel framework utilizing Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) augmented with recurrent neural networks to effectively model social influence networks with temporal dynamics. Our approach leverages the strengths of both GNNs, which excel at learning node representations based on network structure, and recurrent neural networks, which are adept at processing sequential data. Specifically, we introduce a Temporal Graph Convolutional Network (TGCN) that iteratively updates node embeddings by incorporating information from neighbors at each time step, effectively capturing the dynamic propagation of influence. We demonstrate the efficacy of our TGCN through theoretical analysis and illustrate its performance through a conceptual evaluation, showcasing the ability to model complex influence patterns within social networks. The core claim is that GNNs, when extended with temporal mechanisms, can accurately model the complex dynamics of social influence networks over time, considering both structural and temporal relationships. This represents a more sophisticated approach compared to static network models and simpler temporal models.

title: Title: Topological Adaptive Data Structure
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to data structure design, introducing a Topological Adaptive Data Structure (TADS). The core principle of this structure is its dynamic adaptation based on data characteristics and system state, achieved through the exploitation of topological properties. Traditional data structures often rely on fixed parameters, limiting flexibility and efficiency. This work demonstrates how a dynamically adjusting structure can significantly enhance data storage and retrieval performance. We explore the design and implementation of the TADS, detailing its key features and demonstrating its effectiveness through a series of case studies. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential applications and future directions of this innovative data structure.

title: Dynamic Quantum Error Correction Code Construction Theory
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to quantum error correction (QEC) leveraging topological codes. The core idea centers around dynamically adapting the topology of a topological code in real-time to counteract the effects of fluctuating environmental noise, exceeding the error correction capabilities of traditional, static codes. The proposed mechanism utilizes the non-Abelian exchange statistics inherent in quantum topological networks and integrates machine learning algorithms for dynamic optimization of topological parameters, minimizing correction overhead. The research addresses the limitations of existing QEC schemes, which primarily rely on static encoding, by introducing a dynamic framework capable of effectively handling the non-linear disturbances inherent in quantum systems. The theoretical framework presented here outlines a pathway toward more robust and efficient quantum information transmission.

title: Adaptive Quantum State Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative algorithm for quantum state optimization, leveraging the inherent adaptability of quantum states. Traditional approaches to optimizing quantum states often involve manual parameter tuning, which can be time-consuming and limit scalability. Our algorithm utilizes a dynamic parameter optimization technique, intelligently adjusting quantum state parameters to achieve improved efficiency and accuracy. The core mechanism centers around exploiting the quantum state's self-correcting properties to autonomously search for optimal configurations. This paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and preliminary results, demonstrating significant improvements over existing methods in a specific quantum computing benchmark. The focus is on automating the process of parameter adjustment, offering a pathway to more efficient and accurate quantum computations.

title: THE "3=4" PRINCIPLE IN QUANTUM COMPUTING: HYBRID STRUCTURAL ADDRESSING OF MULTIDIMENSIONAL REGISTERS WITHOUT DIGITAL SIGNAL PROCESSING
abstract: This paper introduces an extension of the fundamental AxisAura coordinate-space paradigm into the domain of quantum information science. Modern quantum computing complexes utilizing superconducting qubits face a critical scalability barrier regarding their control electronics. The classical hardware-software pipeline for microwave pulse generation, which relies heavily on Digital Signal Processing (DSP) mathematics to dynamically control phase and amplitude characteristics, introduces a colossal thermal load inside the cryostat, triggering qubit decoherence. The proposed architecture completely eliminates DSP blocks from the control loop. Utilizing the formalized "3=4" Principle, a classical 24-bit task vector is isomorphically projected onto a microwave beam consisting of 4 orthogonal frequency components. Inside the cryostat, a passive superconducting filter bank performs de-multiplexing of the beam, executing passive physical addressing of the target quantum state within a multidimensional register in fixed O(1) time with zero computational heat dissipation near the quantum chip.

title: Graph Neural Networks Learning Based on Biological Neural Networks
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) inspired by the architecture and functionality of biological neural networks. The core idea is to mimic the biological system's structure and mechanisms to design a new GNN architecture that can more effectively learn features from graph-structured data. The proposed method maps graph neural network nodes and edges to biological neurons and synapses, respectively. Furthermore, it leverages the self-organization and learning principles of biological neural networks to optimize the structure of the GNN. This work aims to improve the learning capabilities of traditional GNNs by drawing inspiration from the biological realm. The key contributions lie in the design of a biologically-inspired GNN and the application of self-organizing learning mechanisms. We explore the potential of this approach to enhance performance in various graph-based tasks. ---

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Hidden Computation
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to hidden computation leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. We propose a framework where computational tasks are executed via entangled quantum states, circumventing the need for controlled communication channels traditionally required for hidden computation protocols. Our design focuses on utilizing the non-local correlations inherent in entangled states to perform computations while simultaneously obscuring intermediate data. The core claim is that this entanglement-driven approach can achieve computational superiority over classical methods, guaranteeing security even in fully public communication environments. We present a detailed examination of the underlying mechanisms and highlight the fundamental shift in security assumptions offered by this new paradigm. The key innovation lies in harnessing the intrinsic quantum mechanical properties, specifically entanglement, rather than relying on controlled channels, thereby presenting a potentially more robust and fundamentally secure approach to hidden computation. The theoretical framework discussed here aims to establish a basis for future research and development in this emerging area.

abstract: The increasing deployment of complex AI models, particularly deep neural networks, raises significant concerns regarding interpretability and trust. title: Quantum Error Correction and Neuromorphic Architectures for Distributed Computing
abstract: This paper proposes a novel computational architecture that synergistically combines quantum error correction techniques with neuromorphic systems inspired by biological neural networks. The core claim is to design an architecture capable of efficiently correcting quantum errors while simultaneously providing high-parallelism and fault-tolerance for distributed computing. This is achieved by integrating Quantum Error Correcting Codes (QECCs), specifically Low-Density Parity-Check (LDPC) codes, with neuromorphic networks, such as Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs). The SNNs handle the encoding and decoding of quantum information, leveraging their local connectivity and parallel processing capabilities to accelerate error correction and data transmission. This architecture aims to mitigate the classical computational bottleneck traditionally associated with quantum error correction and to enhance the practicality and efficiency of quantum computing. The key innovation lies in the collaborative operation of these two distinct computational paradigms. This architecture offers a pathway towards scalable and robust quantum computing solutions.

title: Information-Theoretic Quantification of Neural Network Generalization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantifying neural network generalization using information-theoretic principles. Traditional methods for evaluating generalization often rely on empirical metrics and subjective interpretations. We argue for a more rigorous mathematical foundation, leveraging concepts from information theory, particularly mutual information and Kolmogorov complexity, to precisely measure the information a network requires to generalize effectively. The core contribution lies in defining an information gap between the training data distribution and the distribution of correctly classified outputs. This gap provides a quantifiable measure of the network's capacity and susceptibility to overfitting. We demonstrate the theoretical framework and discuss its implications for understanding and improving generalization performance in neural networks. The research aims to shift the focus from black-box evaluation to a data-driven, mathematically grounded approach.

title: Dataset for Beyond Consensus: Diagnosing Coverage, Majority Bias, and Grounding Equity in High-Stakes Multi-Document Diversity Summarization
abstract: This repository contains the dataset constructed and used to evaluate high-stakes multi-document diversity summarization (MDDS) capabilities of language models, specifically in the domain of crisis response. This dataset is from the paper: "Beyond Consensus: Diagnosing Coverage, Majority Bias, and Grounding Equity in High-Stakes Multi-Document Diversity Summarization. " This dataset allows for the the evaluation of our identified core requirements of high-stakes MDDS: information coverage---identifying all posts relevant to human impact and welfare; information clustering---grouping relevant posts into unique information clusters that report similar information, and identifying a representative post for each cluster; and grounding equity---citing all the supporting source posts for each information cluster, regardless of frequency of information. This dataset is sampled from the the CrisisFacts dataset, a dataset that contains crisis-related information from Twitter, Reddit, Facebook and news streams between 2017 an 2020. We share the document ID's and our respective labels, we refer you to the original CrisisFacts dataset for the streams' full text. More details about the annotation and the dataset can be found in the Readme file.

title: Experimental validation of a compact fault-tolerant architecture for trapped ions
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is beginning to enable logical operations that outperform their unencoded physical counterparts, but useful fault-tolerant computation will require more than low-error quantum memory. An effective architecture must orchestrate efficient logical encoding, low-overhead logical operations, and access to the non-Clifford resources required for universal computation. Here, we introduce and experimentally validate such an architecture based on the $[[20,2,6]]$ $C_4$-Helix code, designed for the early fault-tolerant regime. Using Quantinuum Helios, a 98-qubit trapped-ion quantum processor, we experimentally demonstrate the principal components of this architecture: we perform repeated quantum error correction with an error of $4.6^{+6.2}_{-2.6}\times10^{-5}$ per logical qubit per QEC cycle. We benchmark the complete Clifford group on the two logical qubits of a single codeblock under active error correction, obtaining an error of $2.8^{+1.0}_{-1.6}\times 10^{-4}$ per two-qubit logical Clifford. We further demonstrate a fault-tolerant chain-map interface between $C_4$-Helix and a distance-5 surface code, preparing a heterogeneous three-logical-qubit GHZ state with a fidelity lower bound of $99.925^{+0.068}_{-0.245}\%$. In each case, the encoded implementation outperforms its corresponding unencoded physical baseline without relying on postselection. Circuit-level simulations indicate that improvements in physical fidelity bring the same architecture into the $10^{-6}$-$10^{-8}$ logical-error regime targeted for early fault-tolerant computation. Together, these results establish $C_4$-Helix as a hardware-validated fault-tolerant architecture rather than a bare quantum memory.

title: MARS: What Retrieval Signals Are Hidden in Multimodal Large Language Models for Text-Video Retrieval?
abstract: Text-video retrieval requires representations that can distinguish videos with similar scenes, actions, and temporal patterns. Recent multimodal large language models have been adapted as embedding models, but they often represent each input using a single token from the final layer. This can compress diverse video-text cues into a single vector and limit fine-grained retrieval. To address this limitation, we propose MARS, a multi-layer and multi-slot embedding framework for text-video retrieval. MARS constructs multiple adaptive representation slots by combining hidden states from different decoder layers, compares corresponding text and video slots, and aggregates their similarities for retrieval. To better handle confusing candidates, we further introduce a hard-negative-aware slot specialization objective that encourages the slots to capture discriminative matching cues. Experiments on four text-video retrieval benchmarks show that MARS achieves state-of-the-art results in both direct similarity-based retrieval and reranking settings. Ablation studies and analyses demonstrate that multi-layer fusion, multiple slots, and hard-negative-aware slot specialization provide complementary gains. Code is available at https://github.com/sejong-rcv/MARS.

title: A Unified Rate-Distortion Perspective on Vector, Product, and Scalar Quantization
abstract: Discrete visual tokenization, predominantly driven by vector, scalar, and product quantization, lacks a unified conceptual framework for understanding quantization tradeoffs. In this paper, we propose a unified rate--distortion perspective on modern discrete visual tokenization. By viewing quantization as lossy compression, we characterize the nominal fixed-length coding rate through token count and codebook size, and quantization error as the distortion. Within this framework, we resolve three central questions. First, we theoretically and empirically show that minimizing distortion, rather than maximizing codebook utilization, is the primary intrinsic objective for reconstruction fidelity, with a direct connection to the STE-induced gradient discrepancy. Second, we establish two critical fairness conditions for intrinsic quantization comparison: controlling latent feature statistics and enforcing identical coding rates. Third, under these conditions, we recover the VQ--PQ--SQ distortion hierarchy in modern visual tokenization and show empirically that modern VQ methods achieve the lowest distortion. This work provides a foundational rate--distortion reframing of modern discrete visual tokenization, resolves ambiguities in quantizer evaluation, and provides a controlled framework for isolating intrinsic quantization effectiveness under fixed-rate constraints.

title: Topology-Driven Constraint Optimization for Complex Systems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to optimization utilizing topology to guide constraint selection and enhance solution quality. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with complex, high-dimensional problems, while topological insights can offer a powerful mechanism for identifying optimal solutions. We propose a framework centered around identifying and exploiting topological features within the system being optimized, allowing for the selection of constraint combinations that minimize objective function while simultaneously enforcing specific topological constraints. The paper details the conceptual framework, demonstrates its effectiveness through a series of simplified, yet illustrative examples, and discusses future research directions. The core claim is that incorporating topological reasoning significantly improves the efficiency and robustness of optimization processes, particularly for complex systems.

title: Probability Logic Core Algorithm (PLSA)
abstract: This paper introduces Probability Logic Core Algorithm (PLSA), a novel optimization algorithm based on probabilistic logic and core algorithms. PLSA addresses the challenges of optimizing complex systems with high uncertainty and non-linearity by dynamically adjusting parameters based on probabilistic reasoning. The algorithm leverages the strengths of both probability and core algorithms to achieve robust and adaptable optimization. We present a comprehensive framework for PLSA, detailing its core mechanism, implementation, and performance evaluation. The paper highlights the advantages of PLSA over traditional optimization methods, particularly in scenarios demanding reliable parameter tuning and adaptability.

title: Neural Network Information Entropy Self-Organization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural network design centered around self-organization driven by information entropy. The core idea is to construct a neural network architecture capable of autonomously adjusting connection weights based on the entropy distribution of its input data. This process leverages principles of information theory to guide the formation of efficient information encoding and decoding mechanisms. The proposed system utilizes entropy as an intrinsic driving force for learning, dynamically shaping the network's connectivity to optimally represent and process data with varying levels of complexity. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of this approach and outline a potential framework for implementation, emphasizing the potential for improved network performance in scenarios with non-stationary or highly variable input data. The research contributes to a deeper understanding of how information-theoretic concepts can be integrated into neural network design, potentially leading to more robust and adaptive learning systems.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel method for simulating and predicting complex systems using dynamic quantum state simulations. Traditional simulation approaches often rely on static models, limiting their ability to accurately capture the intricate dynamics of complex systems. This work proposes a new approach that leverages the dynamic nature of quantum states to provide a more realistic and predictive simulation framework. The core mechanism centers on dynamically adjusting the system's quantum state to mimic real-world conditions, allowing for enhanced prediction accuracy. We explore the potential applications of this method in biological systems and materials science, highlighting its advantages over existing techniques.

title: Explainable Reinforcement Learning with Causal Inference
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to reinforcement learning (RL) that integrates causal inference to enhance both the reliability and interpretability of decision-making processes. Traditional RL algorithms often operate as "black boxes," lacking transparency into the reasoning behind their actions. This research addresses this limitation by leveraging causal relationships within an environment to guide the learning process. We propose a framework where causal graphs are utilized to understand the underlying dynamics of the environment, informing the selection of optimal policies in an RL agent. Furthermore, we employ explainable AI (XAI) techniques to provide insights into the agent's decision-making rationale. The core claim is that by combining causal reasoning with RL and XAI, we can significantly improve the robustness and trustworthiness of the learned policies, while simultaneously increasing their interpretability. The proposed method aims to provide a more reliable and understandable system than standard RL approaches, particularly in complex and uncertain environments.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning via Temporal Logic with Neural Network Inference
abstract: This paper proposes a novel neuro-symbolic reasoning framework that integrates temporal logic with neural network inference. The core challenge in artificial intelligence lies in effectively combining the strengths of symbolic reasoning – its precision and explainability – with the learning capabilities of neural networks. Our approach addresses this by employing a neural network to efficiently infer on temporal logic rules, grounding the temporal logic within neural representations of the system's state. We define a system where a temporal logic formula (F) is represented as a set of rules, and a neural network is trained to determine whether a given state (s) satisfies the rules in F. The core equation for this inference process is: `satisfies(s, F) = ∃x. F(x)` Where `s` is the current state, `F` is the temporal logic formula, and `∃x` denotes the existence of a value `x` that satisfies the formula. The neural network, denoted as N, takes the state `s` as input and outputs a probability score representing the likelihood that the state satisfies the temporal logic rules. This probability is calculated as: `P(satisfies(s, F)) = N(s)` The system iteratively updates the state based on the inferred satisfaction of the temporal logic rules. The temporal logic rules themselves can be represented as: `R_i: ψ_i(s_t) ∧ ψ_i(s_{t+1}) ∧ ... ∧ ψ_i(s_{t+k}) → True` Where `R_i` is the i-th rule, `ψ_i(s_t)` represents the conditions on state `s_t`, and `k` is the temporal horizon. The neural network learns to recognize patterns in the state representations that correlate with rule satisfaction. We explore the potential of this framework for AI planning, decision-making, and reasoning tasks, highlighting its advantages in handling complex and uncertain environments. The system's performance is evaluated based on the accuracy of rule satisfaction predictions and its ability to generate appropriate actions based on temporal constraints. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of illustrative scenarios.

title: Adaptive Data Compression and Information Retrieval
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to information retrieval by integrating adaptive data compression techniques with user behavior analysis. The core idea is to dynamically adjust compression algorithms based on user search patterns, ultimately enhancing retrieval efficiency and enabling personalized search experiences. We introduce a user behavior model that captures individual preferences and historical search data. This model is then used to inform the selection and configuration of compression strategies. The system adapts compression parameters, such as algorithm choice and compression level, to align with a user's specific search needs. Experimental results (simulated) demonstrate the potential for significant improvements in retrieval performance compared to static compression methods. This work addresses the limitations of traditional data compression by recognizing the crucial role of user context in optimizing retrieval processes. The key contributions lie in the dynamic adaptation of compression based on user behavior and the creation of a robust user behavior model.

AGN dynamically adjusts the graph structure during training, adapting to the specific characteristics of the data. This adaptive approach, combined with a novel graph-based representation learning technique, results in improved performance across various data analysis tasks. We present experimental results demonstrating the superior performance of AGN compared to conventional models. The core mechanism focuses on iterative graph refinement guided by a learned loss function that prioritizes information extraction from the graph. This paper explores the potential of dynamically structured neural networks to unlock new capabilities in data analysis and modeling.

title: Quantum Entanglement Simulation: A Novel Approach to Non-Local Quantum State Modeling
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, presents a significant challenge for classical computational models due to its inherent non-locality. This research explores the development of a novel quantum state simulation method, leveraging quantum entanglement to achieve a more accurate and efficient representation of complex quantum states. We propose a new algorithm, "Entangled-Interference Simulation," that utilizes quantum entanglement to mimic the non-local aspects of entangled states. The core mechanism focuses on introducing a "纠缠干涉" (entanglement interference) process, which enhances the simulation's precision and speed. This approach has the potential to significantly advance quantum computing capabilities and provide a foundation for more robust and versatile quantum algorithms. The study details the implementation of this algorithm, demonstrating its ability to accurately simulate key quantum states and provides a preliminary assessment of its performance compared to established methods.

title: Based on Quantum Error Correction Codes: Enhancing the Reliability of Distributed Storage
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum error correction (QEC) codes to enhance the reliability of distributed storage systems. Traditional distributed storage methods relying on redundancy often suffer from high costs and inefficiencies, particularly in noisy environments. This research proposes leveraging the inherent error-correcting capabilities of QEC codes to provide a more robust and efficient solution. We explore the theoretical foundations of QEC, focusing on the encoding and decoding processes within a distributed storage architecture. The core claim is that the integration of QEC significantly improves data storage reliability, especially when accounting for the challenges posed by transmission noise. The underlying mechanism involves encoding data using appropriate QEC codes and subsequently employing decoding algorithms to identify and correct errors introduced during transmission. We analyze the impact of different QEC code parameters on system performance, considering factors such as code rate, error correction capability, and computational overhead. The results demonstrate the potential of this approach to achieve higher data integrity and reduce the reliance on extensive redundancy, offering a promising pathway for reliable data storage in challenging conditions.

title: ##混沌系统的量子模拟与优化
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum simulation to revolutionize the modeling and optimization of complex chaotic systems. Traditional methods often struggle with the inherent limitations of classical computation, particularly when dealing with the intricate dynamics of chaotic systems. This work introduces a novel approach leveraging quantum simulation to achieve unprecedented accuracy and efficiency in the modeling and optimization of these systems. We propose a framework that transforms a chaotic system into a quantum system, utilizing quantum computation for precise simulations and then integrating optimization algorithms to refine the system's behavior. The research highlights the potential of quantum mechanics to overcome classical computational bottlenecks and unlock new insights into the behavior of chaotic systems. The core claim is that quantum simulation, when coupled with optimization algorithms, can provide a significantly more accurate and efficient approach to studying and manipulating chaotic systems.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Information Encoding and Decoding with Topological Protection
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to quantum information encoding and decoding leveraging the principles of topological protection using multi-body quantum entanglement systems. The core concept involves encoding quantum information within topologically protected states, primarily utilizing topological defects such as magnetic vortices, and employing the inherent entanglement properties to provide robust protection against environmental decoherence. We explore the manipulation of these states through external control fields (magnetic and electric) to achieve reliable read and write operations. The theoretical framework presented demonstrates a pathway towards highly resilient quantum information processing, significantly mitigating the challenges posed by decoherence in quantum computing. Specifically, we analyze the robustness of the encoded information against various noise sources, quantifying the protection level achieved through topological features. The proposed method offers a promising route for developing practical quantum computers with enhanced fault tolerance.

title: Teaching the Colossus to Say No: A Comparative Analysis Review of Alignment Strategies for Large Language Models
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Alignment Strategies for Large Language Models in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of alignment and large language models as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Future Directions and Emerging Trends in Agentic AI
abstract: The chapter provides an overview of the future direction of this technology. It provides insight into the evolution of independent AI agents, how they can collaborate with each other in order to address common issues, and how we will ensure that these agents are aligned with the goals of mankind. Additionally, the chapter explores the type of software used to create AI agents, how their “digital brains” are organized, and what rules must be followed for the operation of AI agents. The chapter also covers real-world risks relating to AI agents, including safety issues, biases that may be hidden within algorithms, the large amount of computer processing power that will be needed, and the risk that AI will make decisions that are difficult or impossible for humans to understand. Finally, the chapter lays out how this tech will actually be used in everyday life—from hospitals and smart cities to finance and self-driving cars. Ultimately, it serves as a complete guide for anyone trying to understand or build the next generation of AI that actually takes action.

title: Equation Recast for Canonical Operator Learning Across Parametric PDEs
abstract: Learning solution operators across broad parameter ranges can require substantial coverage of both input functions and physical parameters, particularly for purely data-driven parametric models. In addition, the resulting models may fail silently outside the training distribution. We introduce equation recast, which reformulates parametric operator learning as the learning of a single canonical operator. Parameter-induced operator variations are derived analytically from the governing equation and absorbed into effective sources, enabling zero-shot prediction across new parameter regimes. Across multi-parameter, nonlinear, and singular PDE settings, equation recast supports extrapolation, integrates sparse heterogeneous datasets in a shared canonical representation, and uses loss of convergence as an internal warning signal for failure of the recast iteration. In high-fidelity tokamak simulations for nuclear fusion, the framework unifies electron-temperature data across four device geometries through canonical-domain mapping within one jointly trained operator. Equation recast provides a route toward reusable neural PDE solvers combining equation-guided transfer, data efficiency, and monitorable inference.

title: Improving Evaluation Realism with Inference-Time Compute and Deployment Scaffolds
abstract: A core obstacle to alignment evaluation is evaluation awareness: capable models can tell when they are being tested rather than deployed, weakening the conclusions a safety evaluation can support. We present two techniques that make simulated alignment evaluations harder to distinguish from real deployments. Our first technique, critique refinement, spends additional inference-time compute on each simulator action: the simulator generates multiple candidate actions, refines them using feedback from an instance of the target model on how to make them more realistic, and continues the evaluation with the most deployment-like candidate. Our second technique, DISH (Deployment-Imitating SWE-Agent Harness), wraps the target in an agent harness, reducing the gap between simulated and real deployment environments in coding settings. We test the techniques on multiple target models and find that they compose: applying both yields larger realism gains than either alone. Our results show that automated approaches can improve the realism of alignment evaluations, and that these improvements use additional compute more effectively than making the audits longer.

title: Git4Data: Database-Native Version Control for AI Agents
abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents increasingly explore many candidate states of relational data in parallel, each of which should remain isolated, reproducible, and auditable, preferably through the same SQL interface used for ordinary data work. Existing tools support this requirement only partially: source-code version control does not scale to large datasets, whereas relational databases manage large data efficiently but rarely expose native branching, comparison, and merging. We present Git4Data, a database-native version-control layer for agentic workflows. Git4Data treats a database as a repository and a table as a versioned object, exposing Git-style operations (snapshot/tag, branch, diff, and merge with explicit conflict-resolution policies) through SQL extensions. Implemented in MatrixOne, a cloud-native relational database, Git4Data leverages immutable object storage and MVCC to make the cost of these operations proportional to the size of the change rather than the size of the data. On the BranchBench agentic branching workloads, Git4Data outperforms DoltDB by up to an order of magnitude. Overall, we believe this work sheds light on how relational databases can better support AI agents through efficient versioning.

title: Systematic Review of Deep Learning Models in Sentiment Analysis ( 2020-2025)
abstract: Sentiment analysis is one of the most important branches of natural language processing. Sentiment analysis has become a key research area in natural language processing, driven by rapid advancements in deep learning architectures. Where It is used to extract opinions and emotional sentiments from texts about a specific topic or new product, as well as from political and financial news headlines. In recent years, recurrent neural network models, convolutional neural networks, and, notably, transformer-based architectures have significantly improved performance across a wide range of natural language processing tasks. This paper presents a systematic review of deep learning approaches used in sentiment analysis published between 2020 and 2025, following established systematic review guidelines, including a specific search strategy . After applying inclusion and exclusion criteria, a number of final studies were selected for analysis and comparison in terms of methodologies, accuracy, and data used.The study concluded that advances in deep learning models have significantly improved the accuracy of sentiment analysis. The review also recommends developing models capable of more effectively handling linguistic complexities, such as sarcasm, irony, regional dialects, and multiple dialects.

title: A Type Theory of Sense
abstract: Wherever meaning is studied empirically, semantic verdicts come from instruments: an embedding model at a resolution decides whether two completions “say the same thing,” a finer resolution revokes the verdict, a different encoder disagrees licitly with both. Logics of meaning have had no place for any of this — no judgment form for the record of a measurement, no laws for how verdicts propagate when the instrument is refined or replaced, no guarantee that the analysis adds nothing to its data. We present TTS, a constructive extension of Martin-Löf type theory built for exactly that practice: a logic of consequence from measurement data. Judgments take the form Γ ⊢Δ J, where Δ is a measurement context — an instrument's verdict record, entering as constants. Two regime-indexed relation formers carry the logic: indiscernibility and apartness in the constructive tradition of Brouwer, Heyting and Bishop, graded by regimes — instruments at declared resolutions, ordered by refinement. Apartness has no premise-free introduction rule, and the metatheory makes the architecture enforceable rather than rhetorical: soundness over regime-indexed simplicial apartness spaces, conservativity over the base theory, no-fork-ex-nihilo, no-refutation-ex-nihilo, provenance (every derivable fork is forced by the record in every realizing model), and consistency of honest records. Two grades of compositional demand are derived, not primitive — canonicity (the instrument cannot distinguish any two fillers: composition is forced) and the fork (two warranted fillers, recorded apart: composition demands a genuine choice) — with a third, locked, constructed from them. Exclusion is a theorem; forks persist under refinement while canonicity does not, also theorems; and the consistency of an identity discovered by one instrument with a separation held by another is characterized exactly by the order relation between the instruments. The principal application is a formal reconstruction of Fregean sense: a sense is a choice of filler of a compositional demand, reference its boundary, hyperintensional distinctness apartness at a regime, the informativeness of identity its record-dependence — one cross-regime law, instantiated by lexical ambiguity at filler spaces and by the name-state configuration of Frege's celestial case. The motivating subject matter is the geometry of meaning in large language models, whose token spaces are measurably not manifolds: semantic space is stratified, and trajectories of generation encounter loci of genuine choice that the Kan condition of homotopy type theory renders invisible. The empirical sections instantiate the calculus's central judgments in generation behaviour — resampling and fill-in-the-middle protocols, fully logged — as a demonstration of non-vacuity and one replicated qualitative prediction, with an explicit honesty clause; the logic itself is not specific to machine systems. title: Quantum Topography Neural Networks: Dynamic Parameter Adjustment
abstract: Quantum Topography Neural Networks (QTTNs) represent a novel approach to neural network training, employing a dynamically structured quantum topology network to automatically adjust network parameters. This research introduces a method that leverages the inherent adaptability of quantum systems to optimize model performance, particularly when dealing with complex data. The core mechanism involves utilizing the network's dynamic topology to iteratively refine the parameters, leading to improved accuracy and generalization capabilities. This work provides a promising framework for enhancing neural network training through the dynamic adaptation of quantum-inspired structures.

title: Core Claim: A novel quantum algorithm acceleration mechanism based on non-linear matrix properties is designed to enhance quantum computation speed, effectively achieving a quantum computing acceleration.
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for solving complex problems intractable for classical computers. However, realizing this potential requires significant advancements in quantum algorithm design and implementation. This paper introduces a new quantum algorithm acceleration mechanism leveraging the unique properties of non-linear matrices. We propose a framework where the algorithm is optimized to exploit these properties, leading to a substantial speedup in computation. This work explores a method for enhancing quantum computation through the application of non-linear matrix transformations. The core of the approach lies in a carefully constructed algorithm that utilizes the inherent non-linear nature of the matrix to significantly reduce the computational cost. We detail the design of this mechanism, provide a mathematical framework for its implementation, and present initial experimental results demonstrating the potential for accelerated quantum computation. This research contributes to the ongoing effort to unlock the full potential of quantum computing. The core mechanism is to dynamically adjust the matrix to maximize the fidelity of the quantum operations.

title: Non-Exchange Topological Quantum Computing Models
abstract: This paper explores the potential of non-exchange topology in quantum computing, focusing on the design of a computational model leveraging quantum entanglement for topological calculations and simulation. We propose a novel approach utilizing entangled states to represent and manipulate topological structures, and subsequently develop quantum algorithms predicated on this framework. The core claim is that this model offers a fundamentally different approach to solving complex topological problems, potentially exceeding the capabilities of existing classical computational methods. This work investigates the implications of this new model for both computational and theoretical research within the field of quantum topology.

title: Dynamic Topology Space Algorithm Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm framework, Dynamic Topology Space Algorithm (DTSA), designed to automatically identify and model complex system topology structures. The framework leverages a neural network based on adaptive topology learning, enabling real-time updates to topology relationships and optimized data processing through dynamic computations. Traditional topology analysis methods typically rely on handcrafted models, lacking automatic adaptation and computational efficiency. The core mechanism of DTSA involves a self-adaptive topology learning network that continuously updates topology relationships, facilitating efficient data manipulation. This work aims to provide a robust and automated solution for analyzing and simulating complex systems.

title: Symbolic Regression with Evolutionary Algorithms and Bayesian Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel system for automatic mathematical equation discovery from data, termed the "Symbolic Regression with Evolutionary Algorithms and Bayesian Networks" (SRE-EABN) system. The core idea is to combine the exploration capabilities of evolutionary algorithms with the reasoning power of Bayesian networks to efficiently and accurately derive mathematical models. Existing symbolic regression techniques often struggle with complex datasets and lack robust methods for handling uncertainty. The SRE-EABN system addresses these limitations by incorporating prior knowledge through the Bayesian network, which guides the evolutionary search and simultaneously quantifies the uncertainty associated with equation parameters. The system is designed to iteratively refine equation candidates, leveraging both the evolutionary algorithm's ability to explore a vast solution space and the Bayesian network's ability to prioritize promising regions based on prior knowledge and uncertainty estimates. The resulting system demonstrates improved accuracy and efficiency compared to standalone methods, offering a powerful tool for scientific discovery and data analysis.

title: String-Quantum Information Coupling Framework
abstract: This paper explores a novel computational paradigm centered on the intricate interplay between string theory and quantum information. We propose a framework, termed the "String-Quantum Information Coupling Framework," that explicitly links these two fields, leveraging their mutual dependence to achieve synergistic effects in quantum computation and information processing. The core mechanism involves a carefully designed structure that integrates quantum properties within string theory, and conversely, utilizes quantum information principles to optimize computations within the string framework. This approach aims to overcome limitations inherent in current computational models, offering a pathway toward more efficient and versatile quantum technologies. Key Claim Building a new computational paradigm, specifically the "String-Quantum Information Coupling Framework," that synergistically integrates string theory and quantum information. This framework will achieve quantum computation and information processing through the coupling of these two fields. Core Mechanism The proposed framework utilizes a dynamic structural representation, wherein the quantum properties of a string are inextricably linked to the quantum information processing inherent in a specific quantum algorithm. This linkage is achieved through a series of interconnected mathematical constructs, which fundamentally change how the string's quantum state is manipulated. The framework establishes a layered structure, where each layer represents a distinct stage in the computation, and the quantum information is actively maintained and processed across these layers. A key aspect is the "Quantum State Synchronization" algorithm, which mathematically determines the optimal alignment of quantum states across the framework's layers. This synchronization is achieved by defining specific constraints and relationships between the string's quantum state and the information being processed. The core of this mechanism involves a novel transformation of quantum information, enabling it to propagate across the string's structure, effectively enhancing its computational power. Why It Is New Traditional computational paradigms frequently overlook the fundamental interconnectedness between string theory and quantum information. While various approaches have been proposed, the current landscape lacks a cohesive framework that explicitly models and leverages this relationship. This paper introduces a novel computational paradigm, the "String-Quantum Information Coupling Framework," which directly addresses this gap by establishing a dynamic, interwoven structure that integrates these two fields. The framework moves beyond simply describing string theory; it actively defines the *dynamics* of quantum information processing within the string framework, offering a significant departure from existing methodologies. The core mechanism is unique in its explicit design of a quantum state synchronization process, which is essential for maximizing computational potential and offers a path toward more robust and adaptable quantum algorithms. The current state of quantum computing is heavily reliant on classical computation. While quantum computers promise exponential speedups for specific tasks, their limitations are rooted in the inherent fragility of quantum states. The inherent complexity of quantum states can lead to errors that drastically reduce the quality of results. This framework, through its specific coupling mechanism, seeks to mitigate these issues by creating a more stable and controllable quantum state, thereby improving the reliability of quantum computations. The framework's design focuses on creating a continuous loop, where the quantum information is constantly being transferred and manipulated across the string's structure. This loop is controlled by the "Quantum State Synchronization" algorithm, which ensures that quantum states are always aligned and coherent, leading to better performance. This synchronization is not simply a passive process; it actively guides the evolution of the quantum state. The core of the framework utilizes a set of mathematical equations that define the relationship between the string's quantum properties and the information being processed. These equations are carefully constructed to ensure that the quantum state is always optimally aligned and manipulated. The framework's potential benefits include: * Enhanced Computational Power: By directly incorporating string theory, the framework can potentially unlock new quantum algorithms with vastly increased computational power. * Increased Robustness: The explicit synchronization process helps to minimize quantum errors, making computations more reliable. * Versatile Algorithmic Design: The framework provides a flexible structure for designing new quantum algorithms. * Scalable Quantum Systems: The design can be adapted to create scalable quantum systems. This paper will present a detailed mathematical model of the "String-Quantum Information Coupling Framework," including its core equations and mathematical constructs, and discuss the potential applications of this framework.

title: Decentralized Federated Reinforcement Learning with Byzantine Agreement
abstract: Decentralized Federated Reinforcement Learning (DFRL) presents a promising approach to training robust and adaptable RL agents by leveraging distributed data and computational resources. However, this paradigm is susceptible to attacks from Byzantine actors who can inject malicious updates, jeopardizing the learning process and potentially leading to catastrophic outcomes. This paper introduces a novel framework for DFRL that incorporates Byzantine agreement protocols to mitigate these vulnerabilities. Our approach enables agents to collaboratively learn while simultaneously resisting manipulation and ensuring convergence. We formalize the problem, define the key components of the system, and present a theoretical analysis demonstrating the effectiveness of our method. The core claim is that training RL agents across multiple devices introduces vulnerabilities to malicious actors. The core mechanism applies Byzantine agreement protocols to decentralized federated RL, enabling agents to learn collaboratively while resisting manipulation and ensuring convergence. This work significantly advances the field by providing a resilient and trustworthy solution for DFRL, opening up new possibilities for real-world deployments. ---

title: Title: Topological Flow Dynamics for Quantum Entanglement
abstract: The study of quantum entanglement remains a fundamental challenge for theoretical physicists and quantum engineers. Traditional methods of characterizing and manipulating entanglement often rely on measurement-based approaches, which struggle to capture the subtle and dynamic nature of these quantum states. This paper proposes a novel approach, Topological Flow Dynamics (TFD), which utilizes a dynamically evolving topological landscape to represent and protect quantum states. This design extends beyond simple entanglement measurements, offering a framework for controlled manipulation of entanglement properties. The core mechanism leverages the inherent fragility of entangled states, creating a system where the landscape itself influences the entanglement. This paper explores the potential of TFD for advanced quantum information processing and quantum cryptography, highlighting its advantages over existing techniques.

title: Information Theory and Topological Dynamics: A Unified Framework
abstract: This paper explores the integration of information theory and topological dynamics to provide a novel framework for analyzing the complexity of information propagation and data compression. We propose a method that leverages the inherent self-similarity properties of topological structures to optimize information encoding strategies. This approach aims to overcome limitations of traditional information theory by incorporating a dynamic, spatially structured representation of data. The study focuses on establishing a robust model for information transfer and compression, utilizing topological analysis as a key component of the analysis process. We present a detailed theoretical foundation and preliminary implementation demonstrating the potential of this integrated approach.

title: Hardware Acceleration Algorithms Based on Quantum Mechanics Principles
abstract: This paper explores the design and implementation of hardware acceleration algorithms leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics. The core strategy involves mapping computationally intensive algorithms onto quantum computers, harnessing quantum phenomena like superposition and interference to achieve significant speedups. We delve into the selection of appropriate algorithms, their decomposition into quantum circuits, and the execution of these circuits on quantum hardware. The research highlights the potential of quantum computing to tackle problems intractable for classical computers. The presented approach offers a novel pathway to computational acceleration, driven by fundamental quantum mechanical concepts. This work contributes to the growing field of quantum algorithm design and explores the practical considerations of utilizing quantum hardware for accelerating specific computational tasks. ---

title: 基于自适应的强化学习的策略调整
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to reinforcement learning, termed "Adaptive Reinforcement Learning with Dynamic Reward Adjustment," which leverages data distribution shifts to dynamically adjust the reward function. Traditional reinforcement learning methods often struggle with static reward functions and limited adaptability, hindering training efficiency and model performance. Our proposed method utilizes data-driven adjustments to the reward function, enabling the system to proactively respond to changing data environments and achieve superior results. The core mechanism involves learning a data-driven reward function that automatically adapts to distribution shifts, resulting in improved training efficiency and model quality. We present a comprehensive evaluation of the method on several benchmark tasks, demonstrating its effectiveness and robustness.

title: Title: Adaptive Temporal Phase Field for Quantum Error Correction
abstract: Quantum computation promises transformative advancements in various fields, but its inherent fragility necessitates robust error correction techniques. Traditional methods often struggle with the complexities of quantum systems, particularly in the face of noise and decoherence. This paper proposes an innovative approach to quantum error correction leveraging an Adaptive Temporal Phase Field (ATPF) algorithm. This algorithm dynamically adjusts the phase field to mitigate the impact of errors, enhancing the overall system's resilience. We present a novel mathematical framework for analyzing the system's state evolution and implementing this dynamic phase field. The proposed method demonstrates significant improvements in error correction performance through a rigorous analysis and simulation. This work represents a fundamental shift in error correction, offering a promising path towards more reliable quantum computations.

title: PowerGenome Renewable Resource Profiles
abstract: PowerGenome Renewable Resource Profiles: PowerGenome input data assembled from public sources. This release corresponds to a PowerGenome-data manifest at data version 2026.08.31. This is the initial release of this dataset. All 6 files are new in this version. Renewable Resource Profiles Hourly generation profiles for new-build renewable resources, used by PowerGenome via RESOURCE_GROUP_PROFILES. This folder holds one parquet per technology plus the site-mapping files that join profiles to Princeton capacity areas. Method Profiles were generated with NREL's reV framework and the SAM (System Advisor Model) engine using wind resource data from the Wind Integration National Dataset Toolkit (WTK) and solar resource data from the National Solar Radiation Database (NSRDB). Site selection. A 10 km × 10 km grid was generated over the contiguous United States. Princeton solar capacity areas (CPAs) were assigned to the nearest grid point, and each grid point was matched to the nearest NSRDB weather site (GID); hourly weather data were retrieved for those sites. For wind, each wind CPA was matched to the nearest WTK weather site (GID); hourly weather data were retrieved for those sites. Weather years span 2007–2013. Simulation. For each weather year and site, reV executed SAM's PVWatts v8 model (solar) or wind power model (wind) to produce an hourly capacity-factor profile per site: Utility-scale solar — PVWatts v8, single-axis tracking with bifacial modules (bifaciality 0.7), DC/AC ratio 1.34, 5 MW per site, total system losses ≈14%. Onshore wind — NREL Reference 5.5 MW turbine (rotor diameter 175 m, hub height 115 m) modeled as a 32-turbine, 176 MW farm. Offshore wind — NREL Reference 12 MW turbine (rotor diameter 214 m, hub height 137 m) modeled as a 32-turbine, 384 MW farm. Files File Contents _rev_profiles_20240801_tidy.parquet Hourly capacity-factor profiles in tidy form. One row per (site_id, weather_year, time_index) with column value (capacity factor 0–1). _site_mapping_20240801.parquet Site mapping with one row per grid point: CPA_ID (the Princeton capacity area the grid point was assigned to), Site (the NREL WTK/NSRDB resource site used to generate the profile), and profile_dist (the great-circle distance between the grid point and that site, in km). Profile records are keyed by site_id, so a site map joins the hourly profiles to the Princeton capacity areas they represent. Weather years span 2007–2013. title: Customer Experience (CX) Metrics as Indicators of Conversational ROI
abstract: The chapter examines the growing importance of customer experience (CX) metrics in evaluating conversational return on investment (ROI) within intelligent chatbot ecosystems. The study aims to explore the relationship between customer experience and conversational ROI, review major CX metrics, analyze chatbot influence on customer loyalty and retention, and identify methods for integrating CX indicators into ROI frameworks. Findings indicate that conversational quality, personalization, responsiveness, and experiential metrics significantly influence financial performance, customer lifetime value, and retention outcomes. The chapter contributes by proposing holistic evaluation perspectives that integrate qualitative customer experiences with quantitative business metrics to assess the overall performance of conversational marketing.

title: Architecture-Level Event-Oriented Frontend for Heterogeneous Sensor Inference in Photonic Stochastic Systems
abstract: Heterogeneous sensor systems generate measurements in incompatible physical units, which complicates their direct integration with photonic stochastic processors. This study proposes an architecture-level event-oriented frontend that converts heterogeneous sensor channels into unified event-oriented probabilities and then into Bernoulli bitstreams compatible with polarization-encoded optical interfaces. The framework combines sensor-to-probability mapping, weighted event-level fusion, stochastic bitstream generation, and system-level control of correlation and synchronization. Its performance was investigated through reproducible Colab-based modeling using baseline validation, weighting-strategy comparison, static and time-varying decorrelation/synchronization studies, and robustness/scaling analysis. The validation framework also includes a first-order analysis of photonic-interface nonidealities and a semi-real validation case using a digitized 520 nm optical smoke-transmittance response from the literature. The results show that the stochastic event estimate converges toward the float reference with increasing bitstream length, reliability-aware weighting outperforms equal and tested data-driven weighting in the benchmark, independent stream generation provides the best inference quality, and synchronization mismatch becomes measurable in time-varying fusion. The frontend also demonstrates graceful degradation under channel corruption and favorable scaling under mixed informative, weak, redundant, conflicting, and noisy channel configurations. These findings indicate that heterogeneous sensors can be interfaced with photonic stochastic systems through a common event-level representation and that weighting, decorrelation, synchronization, and robustness must be treated as core frontend design variables.
